MET-H303.remedy: Params passed validation but the underlying write to the caller's io.Writer failed (disk full, closed pipe, permission denied, ...). Check the destination and retry -- this is an I/O failure on a legal request, not a domain-validation rejection (see MET-H300/H301/H302 for those).

MET-H304.message: perf run requested with months={months}, must be > 0
MET-H304.remedy: Call RunPerf (or perfci's -months flag) with a positive months value. A run driving zero or negative simulated months cannot produce a monthly-tick-time measurement.

MET-H305.message: perf run's AdvanceTicks command (n={n}) was rejected by the engine: {engineErrorCode}
MET-H305.remedy: The engine rejected a command issued by RunPerf's tick-driving loop -- see engineErrorCode for the underlying engine.core rejection. The perf run aborts rather than reporting a partial measurement as if it were complete.

MET-H306.message: perf results file {path} is corrupt at line {line}: {cause}
MET-H306.remedy: An existing perf-results NDJSON file failed to parse as the expected PerfRecord schema. This is distinct from AC-8's 'no baseline yet' case (a missing file is never an error) -- a file that exists but will not parse means the results file itself needs investigating (truncated write, manual edit, format drift) before this preset's baseline can be trusted again.

MET-H307.remedy: M0-ENG §6 point 5, applied since BUG-272 to the PRIMARY, deterministic allocation-based signal (AllocBytes/AllocCount): a commit that regresses either allocation metric more than {threshold} (as a fraction) at the 1M-citizen synthetic fails the build -- allocation counts are identical run-to-run for the same commit (modulo negligible incidental noise, ~0.2% observed), unlike sub-millisecond wall-clock timing on shared CI hardware, so this signal does not flap on runner load. Wall-clock is a demoted ADVISORY check that only contributes to this failure on a GROSS (WallClockGrossRegressionThreshold, e.g. >2x) slowdown, never on ordinary CI jitter. Investigate what the commit changed on the tick path -- a real allocation regression is not a runner-noise artifact the way a wall-clock delta can be.

MET-H308.message: perf record rejected: PhaseHookCount/PerfResult provenance not marked as measured
MET-H308.remedy: AppendResult only persists PerfResult values RunPerf itself produced (Measured=true) -- a hand-built PerfResult (e.g. a bare struct literal from a second writer, a hand-edited re-upload) cannot be distinguished from a real measurement once written, so it is rejected before it reaches the results file rather than silently accepted as if RunPerf had produced it (BUG-055). If this is a legitimate new caller, route it through RunPerf, or construct the record via a helper that explicitly sets Measured=true after confirming the figures really came from a real run.

MET-H309.message: perf CI gate could not evaluate this run: {message}
MET-H309.remedy: BUG-071: CompareToBaseline skipped the percentage regression check (ScaleMismatch or BelowNoiseFloor) rather than genuinely passing or failing -- this is NOT a pass. cmd/perfci exits its distinct could-not-evaluate code and does not record this run's measurement as the new baseline. Since BUG-272, BelowNoiseFloor means the PRIMARY allocation-based signal could not be judged (either side's AllocCount is below MinMeasurableAllocs) -- re-run at a scale the gate can actually judge (matching CitizenCount/Months against the stored baseline, and comfortably above MinMeasurableAllocs) before trusting this commit's perf status either way.

MET-H310.message: perf record for preset {preset} at line {line} is not a plausible genuine measurement: {reason}
MET-H310.remedy: BUG-085: a value like a negative CitizenCount, Months, or PerMonthTick can never be produced by a real RunPerf call (ValidateParams/RunPerf reject these before any measurement begins) -- this record was rejected as untrustworthy provenance even though its Measured flag was set, and LoadLatestBaseline fell back to the last genuinely plausible record. Investigate how this line reached the results file (hand edit, corrupted-cache restore, manual merge-conflict resolution, re-uploaded/edited artifact) -- do not simply re-flip Measured or edit the value to a positive number without understanding how it got there.

MET-H311.message: perf record for preset {preset} sets AcceptedRegression=true with no AcceptedReason
MET-H311.remedy: BUG-083: cmd/perfci's -accept-regression flag (the deliberate, visible way to accept a legitimate slowdown as the new baseline) requires -accept-reason -- a human-readable justification persisted verbatim alongside the accepted measurement. A record claiming an override with no recorded reason is refused as untrustworthy at both the write boundary (AppendResult) and the read boundary (LoadLatestBaseline); re-run cmd/perfci with both flags set to actually accept a regression.

MET-H400.message: could not obtain the weakness-histogram source data: {reason}
MET-H400.remedy: RunWeakness could not exec `node claude-bow.js weakness` or could not parse its stdout into the expected histogram shape. Check node/claude-bow.js are reachable from the repo root, and that its output still matches cmdWeakness's documented shape (claude-bow.js) -- a source that genuinely returned zero findings prints its own known-empty sentinel, which this is NOT that.

MET-H401.message: could not obtain the BOW lint drift report: {reason}
MET-H401.remedy: RunLint could not exec `node claude-bow.js lint` or could not parse its stdout into the expected findings shape. Check node/claude-bow.js are reachable from the repo root, and that its output still matches cmdLint's documented shape.

MET-H402.message: could not obtain sprint {sprint}'s gate status: {reason}
MET-H402.remedy: RunGateStatus could not exec `node claude-bow.js gate-status <sprint>` or could not parse its stdout into the expected per-check/overall shape. Check node/claude-bow.js are reachable from the repo root and that a gate run has actually been recorded for this sprint.

MET-H403.remedy: The perf-results NDJSON file or the accepted-regression registry JSON file existed but could not be parsed cleanly (a torn write, corrupt JSON). This is distinct from the file simply not existing yet, which is not an error -- re-run the perf-CI job or repair/regenerate the named file.

MET-H404.message: failed to write the logged note to the feedback inbox: {path}
MET-H404.remedy: LogNote could not durably write the submitted note (disk error, unwritable inbox directory, marshal failure). The note was NOT filed -- retry the -log command; nothing was silently discarded, but nothing was recorded either until this succeeds.

MET-H405.message: logged note had an empty body
MET-H405.remedy: Pass real note text to -log -- an empty or whitespace-only note is rejected before any file is written, since it would file a useless blank BOW record.

MET-U600.message: method {method} called on a struct-copied Screen (not the *Screen New returned)
MET-U600.remedy: A *menu.Screen value was copied (`s2 := *s`) and a method was then called on the copy. Screen's mu is a sync.Mutex VALUE while subs/stale/saveEntries/settings/settingValues/selectedKeymap are reference types a copy ALIASES, so a copy is a second, independent lock over state meant to be exclusively owned by the original (SEC-020) — this call is rejected fail-closed instead of racing or corrupting the shared state. Fix the caller to hold and pass the single *Screen New returned, never a dereferenced copy of it.

MET-U601.message: malformed {view} patch could not be applied: {cause}
MET-U601.remedy: The patch was not valid JSON for the f10.session view schema (bad JSON, unrecognised schemaVersion, or an oversized payload) and was dropped; the menu screen's session view keeps its last-known-good state (SF-7). If this persists, check the sending engine module's view patch encoding for f10.session.

MET-U602.message: delta for unknown or stale subscription {subscriptionId} dropped
MET-U602.remedy: ApplyDelta received a protocol.Delta whose SubscriptionID was never bound via BindSubscription (or was bound to a view since unsubscribed). This is expected transiently around resubscribe/unsubscribe races; if it persists, check the caller's SubscriptionID-to-view routing (SF-7 — never applied, never a panic).

MET-U603.message: Subscribe called with unrecognised view name {view}
MET-U603.remedy: This screen only subscribes to its one registered view (f10.session). Passing any other name is a programming error at the call site — fix the caller rather than adding a new view name here without updating code.json's outbound edges and this package's doc.go.

MET-U604.message: failed to enumerate the save root
MET-U604.remedy: The injected BundleLister (or the default save-root walk) returned an I/O error reading the save root directory. The save browser renders "unavailable" rather than a stale or empty list (SF-7/MEN-7). Check the configured save root path and the BundleLister wiring.

MET-U605.remedy: A keymap or dashboard-layout profile could not be durably written to disk (encode or write failure). Nothing was silently discarded — the write failed and reported; retry with a writable path. This one code is shared by keymap and layout profile writes (GR#3).

MET-U606.remedy: OpenLayoutEditor could not open the F10 → layouts editor: either no ui.dash editor is wired via WithLayoutEditor, or no layout profile has been loaded/selected. The entry point reports "unavailable" rather than silently no-op'ing or invoking the editor with no profile (MEN-4/MEN-7/SEC-213). Wire ui.dash's (MOD-038) layout editor at construction when it lands, and select/load a profile before opening the editor.

MET-U607.remedy: SelectKeymap was called with a nil keymap or nil grammar. This is a programming error at the call site (LoadKeymapFile parses the profile before selecting, so nil cannot arrive via that path) -- the call is rejected with this registry error rather than a nil-pointer panic inside ui.keys' ApplyKeymap (SEC-079, GR#1). Fix the caller to pass a parsed *keys.Keymap and a constructed *keys.KeyGrammar.

MET-U608.remedy: A keymap or dashboard-layout profile could not be read from disk (file read or JSON/schema parse failure). Nothing was silently invented -- the load failed and reported this registry code; check the path and that the file is valid profile JSON. This one code is shared by keymap and layout profile reads (GR#3), mirroring MET-U605 for writes (SEC-212).

MET-U609.message: failed to read save-slot header for {slot}
MET-U609.remedy: A single save bundle's header.json could not be read (corrupt header.json, an unreadable file, or an incompatible format version). The slot is skipped -- one bad slot must not hide every other save -- and the failure is recorded in SaveListErrors as a registry-sourced error with a correlation ID (SEC-218, GR#7/GR#1). The raw cause (which may carry the save root's absolute filesystem path) is preserved on the error via errors.Unwrap for diagnostics, never surfaced in this message. Re-save or remove the offending slot.

MET-U700.message: malformed {view} patch could not be applied: {cause}
MET-U700.remedy: The patch was not valid JSON for the named f9.* view schema (bad JSON, unrecognised schemaVersion, or an oversized payload) and was dropped; the ticker screen's affected view keeps its last-known-good state (SF-7). If this persists, check the sending engine module's view patch encoding for the named view.

MET-U701.message: delta for unknown or stale subscription {subscriptionId} dropped
MET-U701.remedy: ApplyDelta received a protocol.Delta whose SubscriptionID was never bound via BindSubscription (or was bound to a view since unsubscribed). This is expected transiently around resubscribe/unsubscribe races; if it persists, check the caller's SubscriptionID-to-view routing (SF-7 -- never applied, never a panic).

MET-U702.message: Subscribe called with unrecognised view name {view}
MET-U702.remedy: This screen only subscribes to its four registered f9.* views (f9.ticker, f9.bulletin, f9.annual, f9.archive). Passing any other name is a programming error at the call site -- fix the caller rather than adding a new view name here without updating code.json's outbound edges and this package's doc.go.

MET-U703.message: news story with empty eventId dropped from {view} patch (TIK-5)

MET-G303.remedy: Occupancy/throughput (and residential population) must be finite and non-negative. Reject negative or NaN/Inf occupancy rather than propagating a negative or NaN demand figure (GR#1/GR#16).

MET-G304.message: data/market.json could not be loaded for utility billing from {dir}: {cause}
MET-G304.remedy: Check that data/market.json exists under the resolved data directory and passes engine.market's Load validation (pricingMode "static", all nine commodities present).

MET-G305.message: data/seasonal.json could not be loaded for seasonal modifiers from {dir}: {cause}
MET-G305.remedy: Check that data/seasonal.json exists under the resolved data directory and passes engine.season's Load validation (all eight required curves present).

MET-G306.message: network {network} solve received a negative or non-finite demand of {value} for entity {entity}
MET-G306.remedy: Demand figures must be finite and non-negative before reaching the conserved solve. Reject the figure rather than letting NaN/Inf/negative values poison the delivered + shortfall == demand accounting.

MET-G307.message: network {network} has no solved tick to query a shortfall for
MET-G307.remedy: Run Network.Solve (or UtilityAPI.SolveDailyTick) before querying per-entity shortfall.

MET-G308.message: entity {entity} was not part of network {network}'s most recent solve
MET-G308.remedy: Query shortfall only for entities included in the latest solve's consumer set.

MET-G309.message: source {id} capacity is negative or non-finite: {value}
MET-G309.remedy: Source capacity must be finite and non-negative. Reject the source rather than letting a negative capacity produce a negative delivery (units destroyed) in the conserved solve.

MET-G310.message: edge {from}->{to} length is negative or non-finite: {value}
MET-G310.remedy: Edge length must be finite and non-negative. Reject the edge rather than letting a negative length produce a negative loss fraction.

MET-G311.message: aquifer sustainable yield is negative or non-finite: {value}
MET-G311.remedy: The §17 sustainable-yield ceiling must be finite and non-negative. Reject the aquifer rather than letting a negative yield produce a negative draw.

MET-G312.message: storage {id} capacity is negative or non-finite: {value}
MET-G312.remedy: Storage capacity must be finite and non-negative. Reject the storage node rather than admitting a negative-capacity node.

MET-G313.message: aquifer abstraction request is negative or non-finite: {value}
MET-G313.remedy: AquiferYield.Abstract must be asked to abstract a finite, non-negative amount. Reject a negative or NaN/Inf request rather than returning a negative or NaN draw.

MET-G314.message: demand for {ref} overflowed to a non-finite value after coefficient x occupancy and seasonal modifiers
MET-G314.remedy: A public demand query must never return a non-finite (+Inf/NaN) demand. Reject a coefficient x occupancy (or seasonal-multiplied) result that overflows float64.

MET-G315.message: network {network} solve arithmetic overflowed (demand {demand}, survival fraction {survive})
MET-G315.remedy: The daily-tick solve's supply/loss accumulation overflowed float64. Reject the degenerate configuration rather than masking an Inf-Inf NaN as full delivery.

MET-G400.message: data/logistics.json (or its engine.market dependency data/market.json) could not be loaded or failed schema validation from {dir}: {cause}
MET-G400.remedy: Check that data/logistics.json exists under the resolved data directory and passes foundation.data's schema validation (positive version; each commodity has a non-empty unit, a non-negative throughput, a shortfall factor in (0,1], a non-negative shelf-life and holding-cost, and a defaultBufferPolicy naming a policy present in the file's bufferPolicies map), and that data/market.json passes engine.market's Load. engine.logistics never falls back to a silent default substitution (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G401.remedy: engine.logistics requires all nine §6 commodities (water, power, gas, foodStaples, foodFresh, fuel, constructionMaterials, consumerGoods, waste) present in data/logistics.json's "commodities" map. Add the named commodity — foundation.data's schema validation does not catch this because it has no notion of which commodity keys this consumer needs.

MET-G402.remedy: Query LogisticsAPI only with one of the nine registered commodities (engine.market's CommodityType constants). An unregistered commodity is rejected loudly, never a panic or a silently-created zero-value stock/queue entry (AC-13/GR#7).

MET-G403.message: unknown district "{district}" for commodity "{commodity}": the district has never been provisioned
MET-G403.remedy: Stateful LogisticsAPI operations (Stock/Draw/Restock/SetBufferPolicy/OrderSize) require the (district, commodity) stock to have been Provisioned first. This is the coarse stub's analogue of an unregistered junction ID (AC-13): rejected loudly, never a silently-created zero-value entry.

MET-G404.message: unknown buffer policy "{policy}" requested from SetBufferPolicy
MET-G404.remedy: SetBufferPolicy only accepts a policy name present in data/logistics.json's "bufferPolicies" map (lean/fat at baseline). An unknown tier is rejected, never silently fallback to a default (GR#7).

MET-G405.message: LogisticsAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value, not the one Load/LoadDefault constructed
MET-G405.remedy: Always use the *LogisticsAPI pointer Load returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('l2 := *l') or pass it by value -- that produces a second value with its own mu but ALIASED stocks/subs/cfg state, so the copy's mu protects nothing shared (SEC-020-class, mirroring engine.finance's MET-G204). If you need a second independent API, call Load again.

MET-G500.message: data/buildings.json's "zones" array could not be loaded or failed validation from {dir}: {cause}
MET-G500.remedy: engine.build requires all eight §34 zone types (Dwelling, Shop, Office, Entertainment, Farming, Manufacturing, Heavy Industry, Mining) present in data/buildings.json's top-level "zones" array, each with a non-empty materials bill whose quantities are non-negative, a non-negative labour requirement, and a non-negative baseLeadTimeDays. At Baseline One depth the materials bill must name exactly the "constructionMaterials" commodity. engine.build never falls back to a silent default substitution (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G501.message: unknown zone type "{zone}" submitted to BuildAPI
MET-G501.remedy: Submit zone/build/demand commands only with one of the eight §34 zone types (engine.build's ZoneType constants). An unregistered zone type is rejected loudly, never a panic or a silently-accepted no-op (AC-10/GR#7).

MET-G502.message: cell reference out of bounds (tile {tile}, local {local})
MET-G502.remedy: BuildAPI commands and queries require a tile inside the 30x30 expansion extent and a local cell inside the 200x200 tile grid. An out-of-bounds cell is rejected before any state is touched (AC-10).

MET-G503.message: cell (tile {tile}, local {local}) is not owned by owner {owner}
MET-G503.remedy: A cell cannot be zoned, built on, or demolished before the issuing player owns its tile (purchase it first — US-3/§7). engine.build enforces this gate at command-acceptance time and mutates no zone/queue state on rejection (AC-3).

MET-G504.message: demolish command against cell (tile {tile}, local {local}) with no structure to demolish
MET-G504.remedy: SubmitDemolishCommand requires the cell to already carry a structure (a completed build). A demolish against an empty cell is rejected, never a silently-accepted no-op (AC-10/GR#7).

MET-G505.message: BuildAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value, not the one Load/LoadDefault constructed
MET-G505.remedy: Always use the *BuildAPI pointer Load returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('b2 := *b') or pass it by value -- that produces a second value with its own mu but ALIASED maps/queue state, so the copy's mu protects nothing shared (SEC-020-class, mirroring engine.finance's MET-G204). If you need a second independent API, call Load again.

MET-G506.message: engine.season returned an invalid construction-speed multiplier {multiplier} at month {month}
MET-G506.remedy: The §9 construction-speed multiplier must be a finite value strictly greater than zero. A NaN/Inf/non-positive multiplier would make effective lead time undefined or infinite; engine.build rejects it rather than wrapping or producing NaN/Inf (GR#16 numeric safety).

MET-G507.message: negative month index {month} passed to BuildAPI
MET-G507.remedy: BuildAPI accepts only non-negative absolute month indices (0 = world genesis month, matching engine.core's Clock.Month()). A negative month is rejected before any seasonal or tick computation runs (GR#16).

MET-G508.message: BuildAPI dependency {dependency} is not wired for operation {operation}
MET-G508.remedy: Wire the missing dependency before using the operation: SetWorld before SubmitZoneCommand/SubmitBuildCommand/SubmitDemolishCommand/PurchasePrice, SetSeason before SubmitBuildCommand, and SetLogistics before Tick. engine.build never silently no-ops a command because a dependency was forgotten (GR#1/GR#17).

MET-G600.message: household {household} is not present via CitizensAPI
MET-G600.remedy: Form the household first (engine.citizens' ApplyLifeEventCommand with LifeEventPartner) before querying it through HouseholdsAPI, or pass a household id CitizensAPI actually reports. The query is rejected rather than silently zeroed (AC-10).

MET-G601.message: housing typology {typology} is not one of the loaded HS catalogue entries
MET-G601.remedy: Use a typology id present in data/buildings.json's catalogueSection "HS" entries (e.g. terrace, bungalow, penthouse_tower). The appeal/stock lookup is rejected rather than silently zeroed (AC-10).

MET-G602.message: negative built-stock count {count} reported for typology {typology}
MET-G602.remedy: A stock count is a dwelling-unit quantity and must be non-negative. Report a count >= 0, or 0 to clear the typology's stock (GR#16).

MET-G603.message: HS housing-typology catalogue could not be loaded from {dir}: {cause}
MET-G603.remedy: Check that data/buildings.json is present, valid, and carries catalogueSection "HS" entries with non-empty appealProfile arrays. engine.households never falls back to a silent empty catalogue (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G604.message: HouseholdsAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G604.remedy: Always use the *HouseholdsAPI pointer Load/LoadDefault/NewFromBuildings returned. A copy carries its own mutex over the same aliased stock map (SEC-020).

MET-G605.message: HouseholdsAPI dependency {dependency} is not wired for operation {operation}
MET-G605.remedy: Wire the engine.citizens dependency with SetCitizens before querying household membership/composition/overcrowding/rent-burden. engine.households never silently no-ops a query because a dependency was forgotten (GR#1/GR#17).

MET-G606.message: household {household} references member {member}, which does not resolve via CitizensAPI
MET-G606.remedy: A household's member list must name citizens CitizensAPI actually reports — the conservation invariant's no-orphaned half. Fix the member list (or seed the citizen) rather than silently skipping the orphaned member.

MET-G607.remedy: Rent and income are non-negative monetary quantities in micro-pounds. Pass a value >= 0; zero income is valid and reads as rent-burdened via the citizens sentinel (GR#16/FEAT-086).

MET-G700.message: invalid §11 attractiveness weight {field}={value} (must be finite, in [0,1], and the seven weights sum to 1)
MET-G700.remedy: Fix the weight in the attract config data so each of the seven weights is a finite fraction in [0,1] and they sum to 1 (within 1e-6). engine.attract rejects an invalid weight config rather than silently defaulting to an unweighted or zero-weighted term (AC-10).

MET-G701.remedy: Fix the named config field: the migration rate must be finite and non-negative, the reputation rates finite in [0,1] with fallRate strictly greater than riseRate (the Detroit-trap asymmetry, US-2), reputation.max finite and positive, and aWorld finite. A failed config load is surfaced as this code, never a silent zero substitution.

MET-G702.message: AttractAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G702.remedy: Always use the *AttractAPI pointer New returned. A copy carries its own mutex over the same aliased state (SEC-020).

MET-G703.message: AttractAPI dependency {dependency} is not wired for operation {operation}
MET-G703.remedy: Wire the engine.citizens/finance/households dependency with SetCitizens/SetFinance/SetHouseholds before querying the HousingAffordability term or applying migration. engine.attract never silently no-ops because a dependency was forgotten (GR#1/GR#17).

MET-G704.message: invalid term input {field}={value} (a §11 term must be finite and in [0,100]; rent must be non-negative)
MET-G704.remedy: Pass the five pushed terms as finite values in [0,100] and a non-negative monthly rent in micro-pounds. The input is rejected with no state change (FEAT-086).

MET-G705.remedy: Housing vacancy and junction arrival throughput are non-negative quantities. Pass a value >= 0; the migration command is rejected with no state change (FEAT-086).

MET-G706.message: the §4 world-pool seam is absent: A_world (the attractiveness comparison baseline) is missing or unloadable
MET-G706.remedy: Supply a WorldPool (e.g. NewStaticWorldPool from a config aWorld field). engine.attract refuses to construct rather than silently defaulting to A_world = 0, which would make any positive A read as attractive regardless of world conditions (AC-11). A genuine zero baseline is expressed as StaticWorldPool{0}, not a nil pool.

MET-G707.remedy: Pass a non-negative simulation month to ApplyMigration. The month keys the per-resident emigration hash stream and the once-per-month reputation advance; a negative value is rejected rather than wrapped into a migrant birth-month or stream key (FEAT-086).

MET-G800.remedy: compose.Wire was called on a *core.Engine that already has PhaseHooks registered. The composition root is the only real hook registrar, so a non-zero hook count on entry means the engine was already composed; construct a fresh engine instead of wiring a second time (AC-3).

MET-G801.remedy: A required module's construction or wiring failed (e.g. market.LoadDefault could not load data/market.json). Check the named module's data file and construction path; compose.Wire returns this without leaving a partially-wired engine (AC-4).

MET-G802.message: composition root: required module {module} is missing from the wired set
MET-G802.remedy: A required module was silently absent from the composition (registering N-1 of N required modules). Every module in the declared required list must construct and register; a quiet partial wiring is a distinct failure, never a success (AC-4).

MET-G803.message: composition root: wiring after engine sealed (module {module})
MET-G803.remedy: compose.Wire was invoked after the Engine sealed its hook set (the first AdvanceTicks already ran). Wire hooks before the first AdvanceTicks call; the original core.ErrEngineSealed cause is preserved via errors.Unwrap (AC-6).

MET-G804.remedy: A gameplay-command rejection pass-through: another module (e.g. engine.world's PurchaseTile) already rendered its own registry-sourced Display string. compose re-wraps it under this code, whose template is exactly {display}, rather than re-rendering it under the foreign module's own code with mismatched ctx keys (BUG-267).

MET-G805.message: composition root: sequential citizen id {id} reached the migrant id namespace (base {base})
MET-G805.remedy: compose's sequential migrant/seed citizen id counter (simState.nextCitizenID) must stay strictly below attract.MigrantIDBase (2^62) — the disjoint high-bit namespace engine.attract mints admitted-migrant citizen ids from (migration.go). This is the FIRST of three disjoint id ranges: compose seeds/direct ids [1, 2^62), engine.attract migrant ids [2^62, 2^63), engine.citizens fertility-born child ids [2^63, ...) (citizens.FertilityChildIDBase). Corrected 2026-08-18 (destructive-review REJECT, FEAT-169): the original guard bounded against FertilityChildIDBase alone, which would have let compose's counter silently drift into attract's migrant range first without tripping this check. This guard fires before compose ever mints a colliding id rather than allowing silent id reuse. No plausible baseline-one population reaches this bound — seeing this error means the counter's growth assumption itself needs re-examining (FEAT-169 ICD §12 open decision 2, amended).

MET-G806.message: composition root: id-namespace ranges overlap (fertilityChildIDBase={fertilityChildIDBase}, migrantIDBase={migrantIDBase})
MET-G806.remedy: Wire-time assertion (FEAT-169 destructive-review REJECT finding): citizens.FertilityChildIDBase must be at least 2x attract.MigrantIDBase so the three-package disjoint id map (compose seeds [1, 2^62), attract migrants [2^62, 2^63), citizens fertility children [2^63, ...)) actually holds. This should never fire in production -- both sides are compile-time constants -- but a future edit to either package's base constant that breaks the convention now fails loudly at every Wire call instead of silently overlapping the two id ranges (the original bug: both bases independently started at 1<<62). See citizens/doc.go and compose/doc.go for the full id map.

MET-G807.message: extcommute finance seam rejected a non-positive money amount ({amount} micropounds) for {verb}
MET-G807.remedy: A FinanceSeam verb (RecordOffMapWage/RemoveOffMapWage/RecordBusinessRates/RecordCorpShare/RecordWageLeakage) was called with a negative amountMicropounds. A negative amount posted through the debit/credit pair would reverse the credit flow (money conservation, GR#16) -- the seam rejects it loudly instead of posting a sign-flipped transaction. Fix the caller (engine.extcommute) so it never derives a negative wage/amount.

MET-G900.message: data/unlock_trees.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation from {dir}: {cause}
MET-G900.remedy: Check that data/unlock_trees.json exists under the resolved data directory and passes foundation.data's validated-load schema (version present; a non-empty meta.categories matching the tree count; every node id globally unique and matching the building-id pattern; a known node kind; in-range tier and prereqTier; every prereqNodeIds edge resolving; and an acyclic prereq graph). engine.unlocks never falls back to a silent default tree set (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G901.message: gate check or spend command referenced an unregistered {kind} "{ref}"
MET-G901.remedy: A gate check, node-unlock query, or SpendDevelopmentPoints named a node id, milestone tier, or category that is not present in data/unlock_trees.json (a typo'd node id or an out-of-range tier index). Fix the reference — this is a typed error, deliberately never a silent 'not unlocked' false negative indistinguishable from a genuine gate failure (AC-12).

MET-G902.message: spending {cost} Development Points on node {node} exceeds the unspent balance {balance}
MET-G902.remedy: The node's dpCost exceeds the current Development-Point balance. Earn more DP (cross a milestone) before spending, or pick a cheaper node (AC-7).

MET-G903.message: node {node} requires milestone tier {tier}, but the current tier is {current}
MET-G903.remedy: The node's prereqTier has not been reached. Cross the prerequisite milestone (advance population past its §4 threshold) before spending Development Points on this node (AC-7).

MET-G904.remedy: BuyOffMapCapacity/OffMapCapacity only accept the five §22 kinds (grid, gas, rail, port, water). Pass one of those, or treat the returned error as a typo at the call site (AC-9).

MET-G905.message: operation {operation} requires a wired engine.finance dependency
MET-G905.remedy: Wire engine.finance via SetFinance before the operation. This module never silently no-ops a cash award or a capacity purchase just because the dependency was forgotten (GR#1/GR#17).

MET-G906.message: ForceUnlock requires debug mode; {capability} is unreachable until debug is enabled
MET-G906.remedy: ForceUnlock is debug-gated (M0-ENG §3). Enable debug mode (feat.debugmode) and wire the debug authorizer via SetDebugGate before invoking it; a debug-gated cheat never runs partially or invisibly with debug off (AC-11).

MET-G907.remedy: A ForceUnlock target must name exactly one of a valid milestone tier (1-13) and a valid tree node id — never neither, never both (AC-11).

MET-G908.message: UnlocksAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value, not the one Load/LoadDefault constructed
MET-G908.remedy: Always use the *UnlocksAPI pointer Load returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('u2 := *u') or pass it by value — that produces a second value with its own mu but aliased maps, defeating the concurrency-safety invariant (SEC-020-class). If you need a second independent API, call Load again.

MET-G909.remedy: An XP award, Development-Point amount, population, or other quantity was negative where only a non-negative value is meaningful. Fix the caller — negative inputs are rejected rather than silently wrapped (GR#16).

MET-G910.remedy: SpendDevelopmentPoints was asked to unlock a node that is already in the unlocked set. The DP balance is left untouched rather than silently drained a second time (GR#1); check the current unlock state before spending.

MET-G1000.remedy: data/freight.json (or the data/market.json or data/logistics.json it loads through the registered engine.market/engine.logistics edges) could not be read or failed validation. Inspect the named field and rule in the error context and correct the data file — freight never falls back to a partial config or a silent default.

MET-G1001.message: port capacity queried with no berths configured
MET-G1001.remedy: The loaded port config carries zero berths — the port is not yet built, so there is no throughput, customs capacity, or saturation to report. Configure at least one berth in data/freight.json (or build one at runtime once berth construction exists) before querying port figures.

MET-G1002.remedy: A stage/movement/storage/trade query named a commodity ID that is not one of the loaded data/freight.json commodities. Check the spelling against data/freight.json's "commodities" map — freight never silently creates a zero-value commodity entry.

MET-G1003.remedy: A chain query named a stage ID that is not one of the loaded data/freight.json chain stages. Check the stage id against data/freight.json's "chains" — freight never silently creates a zero-value stage.

MET-G1004.remedy: A storage query or movement named a storage-site type that is not one of the four documented types (quayside/silo/tankFarm/coldStore). Use a documented site type — freight never silently creates a zero-value site.

MET-G1005.message: storage type mismatch: commodity {commodity} ({commodityClass}) does not match site {site} ({siteClass})
MET-G1005.remedy: The commodity's storage class does not match the site's commodity class (e.g. grain to a tank farm, fuel to a silo). Route the commodity to its matching site type (or add an explicit override once one exists) — a mismatched store is rejected, never silently accepted.

MET-G1006.message: movement tonnage {tonnes} exceeds the {mode} modal cap (max {max})
MET-G1006.remedy: A movement/import/export command declared a tonnage above the mode's documented per-movement bulk cap (road 25t, rail 1,000t, sea 40kt) or below the sea minimum (3kt). Split the movement or choose a higher-capacity mode — over-cap tonnage is rejected, never silently clamped.

MET-G1007.remedy: A movement/import/export/store command declared a negative tonnage. Negative quantities are rejected rather than silently ignored (GR#16) — fix the caller.

MET-G1008.message: FreightAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value, not the one Load/LoadDefault constructed
MET-G1008.remedy: Always use the *FreightAPI pointer Load returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('f2 := *f') or pass it by value — that produces a second value with its own mu but aliased maps/slices, defeating the concurrency-safety invariant (SEC-020-class, mirroring engine.finance's MET-G204). If you need a second independent API, call Load again.

MET-G1009.remedy: data/factorytypes.json (feat.factorytypes, FEAT-105) could not be read or failed schema validation: a missing/zero footprint, an absent or non-positive jobs count, an unknown blight-class enum value, a wrong JSON type, a dangling stageRef into data/freight.json, an inline input/output referencing an unregistered freight commodity, or a stageRef entry that also carries a duplicate inline copy of input-output/jobs/power/water/blight (AC-5/ASM-680). Correct the data file — freight never falls back to a partial or default-substituted factory-type catalogue.

MET-G1010.remedy: A factory-type resolve named a key that is not one of the eight modelled types (assembler/steelMill/electronics/chemicalsConverter/foodProcessing/textiles/cement/glass). Check the key against data/factorytypes.json — freight never silently creates a default-substituted factory-type parameter set.

MET-G1100.remedy: The scenario's shock type must be a recognised ShockType (majorEmployerClosure) and any shock target must name an in-extent, in-bounds cell. The malformed field is named and the scenario is rejected outright — never run with a silently-ignored or silently-substituted shock (AC-11).

MET-G1101.message: recovery command rejected: no decay state on {cell}
MET-G1101.remedy: A demolition/investment/tax-relief command targeted a cell (or district) with no decay state. Recovery of a healthy cell/district is rejected via CommandResult/ErrorRef rather than silently succeeding for free (AC-12).

MET-G1102.message: ghost-city threshold reached with no qualifying warning on record (population {population}, historic peak {historicPeak})
MET-G1102.remedy: The ghost-city death condition requires a qualifying MarginToGhostCity entry in engine.projections' WarningLedger, recorded at least MinWarningLeadMonths before the trigger month (FEAT-068, AC-15). Without one the trigger cannot fire — the gate rejects rather than silently declaring game over (AC-17).

MET-G1103.message: DecayAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value, not the one New constructed
MET-G1103.remedy: Always use the *DecayAPI pointer New returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('d2 := *d') or pass it by value — that produces a second value with its own mu but aliased decay/event/history state, defeating the concurrency-safety invariant (SEC-020-class).

MET-G1104.remedy: A month before the world's epoch (month 0 = genesis) was supplied. Rejected rather than folded into the append-only history, which would corrupt the population provider and the epilogue timeline (AC-13).

MET-G1105.message: required dependency {dependency} not wired for operation {operation}
MET-G1105.remedy: Set the dependency via SetFinance (insolvency death condition) or SetProjections (ghost-city warning gate) before the operation that needs it. Registry-sourced, never a silent no-op or a nil-pointer panic (GR#1).

MET-G1106.remedy: Fix the embedded spiral.json (malformed JSON, a non-positive coefficient, or an unreachable blight frontier). The package fails loudly rather than defaulting (GR#15/GR#7, ASM-241).

MET-G1107.message: negative population {population} rejected at the month boundary
MET-G1107.remedy: A month's population input was negative — a caller bug. Rejected before it reaches the death evaluator, where a negative value would read as 'below 10% of historic peak' and fire a spurious ghost-city game-over (SEC-087).

MET-G1200.remedy: data/services.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation (missing file, malformed JSON, non-positive wage/severity field, empty staffing-pool member list), or a service kind references a Pie benchmark id absent from the pie table. Fix the data file; every failure is registry-sourced, never a silent default substitution (AC-11).

MET-G1201.remedy: RegisterService was called with a ServiceKind that has no KindDef. Register the kind first via ServicesAPI.RegisterKind (the extensible-kind registry, AC-2), or fix the typo — an unregistered kind is rejected rather than treated as an empty service (AC-11).

MET-G1202.remedy: A query or command addressed a ServiceID that RegisterService never registered. Register the instance first, or fix the id — a query for a missing service returns this error, never a zero-value capacity/quality silently presented as an empty service (AC-11).

MET-G1203.message: funding level {level} for service {service} is outside [0,1]
MET-G1203.remedy: SetFunding requires a funding fraction in [0,1]. A value below 0 or above 1 is rejected with this error, never silently clamped without the caller knowing a clamp occurred (AC-12).

MET-G1204.message: service {service} enabling building (tier {milestone}) is not unlocked
MET-G1204.remedy: SetFunding was called for a service whose enabling building's §4 milestone tier has not been reached. The tier gate is the injected UnlockGate (the seam engine.unlocks implements); wire a real gate via SetUnlockGate before funding (AC-7).

MET-G1205.message: staffing pool {pool} is not declared in services.json
MET-G1205.remedy: SetPoolStaff or AllocateStaffing referenced a staffing-pool id absent from data/services.json's staffingPools table. Declare the pool there, or fix the id (AC-4).

MET-G1206.message: service {service} has no further upgrade step
MET-G1206.remedy: Upgrade was called on a service already at the final step of its upgrade path (or with an empty path). Check UpgradePath before upgrading; the ceiling is left unchanged rather than silently advanced (AC-9).

MET-G1207.remedy: RegisterService was called with a ServiceID already present. Registration is rejected rather than silently overwriting the existing instance's capacity/funding/upgrade state (GR#3: no silent last-write-wins).

MET-G1208.message: ServicesAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G1208.remedy: Always use the *ServicesAPI pointer New/Load returned. Dereferencing-and-reassigning (a2 := *a) produces a second value with its own mutex but aliased maps, defeating the concurrency-safety invariant (SEC-020-class). If you need a second API, call New/Load again.

MET-G1209.message: command input {field} is not finite (NaN or ±Inf)
MET-G1209.remedy: A command handler received a NaN or infinite float where only a finite simulation-state value is meaningful (funding level, demand, demand distance, staffing need, or pool availability). Reject the input at the boundary rather than storing it — a non-finite value would otherwise collapse silently inside the quality/staffing arithmetic (SEC-093).

MET-G1210.message: net fiscal cost clawback overflowed (gross {gross}, rate {rate})
MET-G1210.remedy: NetFiscalCost's gross-wage × income-tax-rate intermediate product overflowed int64, so the clawback (and therefore the honest net) cannot be computed. The gross wage bill is too large for the fixed-point arithmetic to represent its tax clawback; reduce the staffing/wage magnitude or surface the figure differently (SEC-094).

MET-G1211.message: district {district} has never had demand pushed
MET-G1211.remedy: CoverageForDistrict or UpdateDistrictDemand was called with a district identity that has never been seeded via UpdateDistrictDemand. Never a zero-value coverage silently read as an empty-but-existing district (AC-23).

MET-G1400.remedy: data/firms.json could not be read or failed this module's schema validation (missing file, malformed JSON, a non-positive or out-of-order stage minStaff, an unknown stage/premise-class slug, a negative founding/credit coefficient, an empty or non-monotone base-rate cycle). Correct the named field and rule in the error context — engine.firms never falls back to a partial config or a silent default.

MET-G1401.message: founding or hiring referenced an unknown citizen ID {citizen}
MET-G1401.remedy: The CitizenID does not resolve through CitizensAPI (AC-15). Reject it rather than silently creating a placeholder citizen — the caller must supply a real citizen record that already exists in the population.

MET-G1402.message: command or query referenced an unknown firm ID {firm}
MET-G1402.remedy: The FirmID is not registered in this FirmsAPI. Reject it rather than silently creating a zero-value firm — found firms before growing/failing/acquiring/querying them.

MET-G1403.message: FirmsAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G1403.remedy: Always use the *FirmsAPI pointer Load/LoadDefault returned. Dereferencing-and-reassigning (f2 := *f) produces a second value with its own mutex but aliased maps/slices, defeating the concurrency-safety invariant (SEC-020-class). If you need a second API, call Load again.

MET-G1404.remedy: A growth attempt could not advance the firm (staff roster below the target stage floor, or no premises secured — AC-4/AC-7). The firm stays at its current stage; supply the missing real hires or grant premises and retry. Never a silent stage advance.

MET-G1405.message: firm {firm} is already at Enterprise stage
MET-G1405.remedy: A growth command targeted a firm already at Enterprise (there is no further stage to advance to, AC-16). Reject rather than silently clamping or ignoring — the command is a no-op and should not be issued.

MET-G1406.remedy: A staff-count query/command carried a non-positive count (AC-16). Supply a positive real-hire list — engine.firms never silently clamps a zero/negative staff count into a plausible one.

MET-G1407.message: firm {firm} cannot secure premises of class {zone}
MET-G1407.remedy: The firm's target-stage premises (right zone class, right size) are not available through engine.build, so growth is blocked and the firm enters the stalled/exit state (AC-7, §45's 'dies or leaves'). Zone the required premises through engine.build, then retry growth.

MET-G1408.message: credit request for {amount} exceeds deposit-backed lending capacity {capacity}
MET-G1408.remedy: The requested loan principal is larger than the bank's deposit pool can back (AC-13). Reduce the request or grow the deposit base — credit cannot be created beyond what the deposit pool and rate cycle would realistically support.

MET-G1409.message: operation {operation} invoked before dependency {dependency} was wired
MET-G1409.remedy: The operation needs a sibling module (engine.citizens/finance/market/build) that has not been wired via SetCitizens/SetFinance/SetMarket/SetBuild. Wire the dependency at composition-root time before running firm lifecycle operations — never a silent no-op (GR#17).

MET-G1410.message: credit request carried a non-positive principal {amount}
MET-G1410.remedy: A firm credit request must carry a positive principal. Reject a non-positive amount rather than silently clamping it to a plausible one — a zero/negative principal is a caller error, not a credit decision.

MET-G1411.message: hire list contains citizen {citizen} already on firm {firm}'s roster
MET-G1411.remedy: A firm's staff roster is a SET of real CitizenIDs (AC-4) — the same citizen cannot be hired twice into one firm. Reject the duplicate hire rather than silently deduping it into a smaller headcount (which would let a firm fake its staff floor, SEC-101).

MET-G1412.message: RemoveFirm targeted an unknown firm ID {firm}
MET-G1412.remedy: RemoveFirm is the compensating inverse of RegisterFirm — it can only undo a registration that actually happened. Reject an unknown FirmID rather than silently succeeding, or a caller would believe it had unwound a registration it never made and a refused win could leak a firm (SEC-159).

MET-G1300.message: data/tax_instruments.json could not be loaded or validated (dir {dir}): {cause}
MET-G1300.remedy: The six-instrument tax set failed to load. Check that data/tax_instruments.json exists, is valid JSON, and passes foundation/data's schema validation (version, the six accepted instrument IDs, valid categories, rate ranges, elasticity, bearer shares summing to 1.0, zone-override keys inside the 8-way enum). Set METROPOLIS_DATA_DIR to override the resolved data directory.

MET-G1301.message: tax instrument {instrument} rate {rate} is outside its valid range [{min}, {max}]
MET-G1301.remedy: SetRate validates the requested rate against the instrument's data-loaded rateRange (data/tax_instruments.json). The rate is rejected — never clamped or silently accepted — and the instrument's current rate is left unchanged. Choose a rate within the declared bounds.

MET-G1302.remedy: The instrument key is not one of the six loaded from data/tax_instruments.json. Check the key against the loaded set (TaxAPI.Instruments). Never treat an unknown key as a zero-value instrument.

MET-G1303.message: tax instrument {instrument} rate is not finite (NaN or ±Inf)
MET-G1303.remedy: A headline rate must be a finite number. NaN or ±Inf would otherwise collapse inside the elasticity/revenue arithmetic; reject it at the boundary rather than storing it.

MET-G1304.message: tax instrument {instrument} base cannot be negative (got {base})
MET-G1304.remedy: Money is never negative (M0-ENG §1.2). SetBase rejects a negative full base rather than storing it.

MET-G1305.message: tax instrument {instrument} EV-share must be a finite number in [0,1] (got {share})
MET-G1305.remedy: The EV-share (base-erosion) input is the fraction of the base eroded by external substitution (e.g. EV adoption eroding fuel-duty revenue). It must be finite and in [0,1].

MET-G1306.message: tax instrument {instrument} district {district} rejected an invalid rate multiplier {multiplier}
MET-G1306.remedy: A district rate multiplier scales the citywide base rate (1.0 = no change, 0 = a tax-free district). It must be a finite number >= 0 whose effective rate (citywide rate × multiplier) stays within the instrument's data-loaded rateRange, and the district ID must be non-empty. Reject — never store — an invalid multiplier (SEC-098: an unbounded district multiplier would blow the effective-rate cap at district level and make revenue non-monotonic).

MET-G1307.message: unknown zone class {zone} in the zone-scoped property-tax computation
MET-G1307.remedy: BusinessRateRevenue accepts only §34's closed 8-way zone-class enum (dwelling, shop, office, entertainment, farming, manufacturing, heavyIndustry, mining). Reject any other key rather than treating it as a no-discount zone.

MET-G1308.message: engine.finance is not wired (call SetFinance first) — {operation} requires it
MET-G1308.remedy: Collect/CollectAll/CollectedRevenue need the wired *finance.FinanceAPI to post ledger transactions or read tax revenue. Wire it via SetFinance; never silently no-op when absent.

MET-G1309.message: TaxAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G1309.remedy: Always use the *TaxAPI pointer Load/LoadDefault returned. Dereferencing-and-reassigning (a2 := *a) produces a second value with its own mutex but aliased maps, defeating the concurrency-safety invariant (SEC-020-class). If you need a second API, call Load/LoadDefault again.

MET-G1500.remedy: crime.json (embedded) is malformed or failed engine.crime's schema validation — a non-positive base rate, a negative driver elasticity, a non-concave deterrence half-saturation, a formation/threshold/lead-window value outside its documented positive range, or a threshold ordering violation. Correct the named field; engine.crime never falls back to a partial config or a silent default.

MET-G1501.message: district {district} is not registered with engine.crime (no AdvanceMonth or RegisterDistrict has introduced it)
MET-G1501.remedy: Query or command only districts the composition root has registered (via AdvanceMonth or RegisterDistrict). engine.crime refuses to fabricate a zero-valued district entry, so an unregistered district is an error, not an empty read (AC-14).

MET-G1502.message: citywide strategy mix rejected: no Constabulary Headquarters built (a station or Divisional HQ does not unlock the citywide patrol/detective/community mix)
MET-G1502.remedy: Build the Constabulary Headquarters (the top command-ladder rung) before setting the citywide strategy mix. The gate is a hard rejection, never a silently-dropped or auto-applied command (AC-10).

MET-G1503.message: strategy mix invalid: patrol+detective+community weights {sum} do not sum to the documented total {total}
MET-G1503.remedy: Set the three citywide weights so they sum to the documented total (crime.json mixTotal). The weights are rejected outright, never silently renormalised (AC-15).

MET-G1504.message: decapitation rejected: no gang with id {gang} exists
MET-G1504.remedy: Decapitate only a gang id returned by GangIDs (a formed, tracked gang). A decapitation command against a nonexistent id is a typed error, never silently ignored (AC-15).

MET-G1505.message: CrimeAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value, not the one New constructed
MET-G1505.remedy: Call methods on the *CrimeAPI returned by New, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's maps/mutex and would race.

MET-G1506.message: prison-intake cross-check requested before a PrisonIntake ledger was wired
MET-G1506.remedy: Wire the (future) engine.prison intake ledger via SetPrisonIntake before calling VerifyPrisonIntake. The cross-check is against an independent ledger, never this module's own say-so (AC-12).

MET-G1507.remedy: Supply finite, non-negative driver/justice inputs for the named district field. engine.crime validates every numeric input at every entry point and rejects a non-finite or negative value with no state change (GR#16).

MET-G1600.message: data/farmtypes.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {field}: {rule}
MET-G1600.remedy: Check that data/farmtypes.json exists at the resolved data directory, is well-formed JSON, has a positive "version", contains all five §31 facility types (arable/livestock/orchard/marketGarden/vineyard), and that every entry has a positive footprintCells, a named chain commodity, a recognised chain destination (mill/dairy/abattoir/packhouse/winery), a recognised soil band and terrain, and non-negative per-variant stocking densities (livestock only). The farm-type catalogue never falls back to a silent default or a partially loaded set (GR#15/GR#7/GR#16).

MET-G1601.message: unknown farm-type key {typeKey} resolved from the farm-type catalogue
MET-G1601.remedy: Resolve only with one of the five §31 facility category keys (arable, livestock, orchard, marketGarden, vineyard). A named crop/livestock (wheat, dairy, apples, vines, …) is a VARIANT within its category, not a top-level farm-type key — resolve the category and read its variants.

MET-G1800.message: data/education.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation (dir {dir}): {cause}
MET-G1800.remedy: Check that data/education.json exists at the resolved data directory, is well-formed JSON, has a positive "version", declares an entryAgeMonths key for every pipeline stage, and carries finite in-domain baselineQuality/attainmentScale/researchPointsPerGraduate/hallsCapacity/dropoutRate values. The education balance set never falls back to a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G1801.message: stage {stage} is not registered as a service instance
MET-G1801.remedy: Call RegisterStages (after wiring engine.services) before issuing a stage-funding command or a stage query. A stage that was never registered is rejected, never answered with a silently zero-valued enrolment/funding figure (AC-12).

MET-G1802.message: citizen {citizen} has no valid age/stage-history state
MET-G1802.remedy: Enrol/transition only citizens that exist in engine.citizens with a non-negative derived age. A citizen with no record or a negative age is rejected rather than silently enrolled with a zero-value record (AC-12).

MET-G1803.message: fork command sums to {sixthForm}+{technical}+{leaveAt16}, but the eligible secondary cohort is {eligible}
MET-G1803.remedy: The three branch counts of an ApplyFork command must sum exactly to the secondary cohort's full eligible size. A mismatch would silently vanish (or invent) a pupil, so it is rejected at the write boundary (AC-13).

MET-G1804.message: stage-funding command for {stage} (fuseYears {fuseYears}) has no projected-consequence payload
MET-G1804.remedy: Every education funding decision's principal effect lands more than five game-years out (A5/§27), so attach a non-empty ProjectedConsequence to the funding command. This module's own pre-submission check rejects an empty payload before it reaches engine.projections (AC-9).

MET-G1805.remedy: Set the funding level within the documented [0,1] range. A level outside it is rejected rather than silently clamped (AC-1).

MET-G1806.message: EducationAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value, not the one New constructed
MET-G1806.remedy: Call methods on the *EducationAPI returned by New/Load, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's maps/mutex and would race.

MET-G1807.remedy: Wire the named outbound dependency via its Set* method (SetCitizens/SetServices/SetSeason/SetTraffic/SetProjections) before invoking an operation that consumes it. A missing dependency fails loudly rather than no-op-ing (GR#20).

MET-G1808.message: RemovePupil called for citizen {citizen} with out-of-range DepartureReason {reason}
MET-G1808.remedy: Use one of the three documented departure reasons (deceased, emigrated, dropped out). An unknown/out-of-range reason is rejected at the write boundary before the pupil is removed, so the live enrolled count and the independent ledger replay can never diverge (AC-10).

MET-G1809.message: stage-funding command for {stage} has a non-finite or non-positive FuseYears tag {fuseYears}
MET-G1809.remedy: Set FuseYears to a finite, positive value. A degenerate tag (NaN/±Inf/<=0) is rejected before the Slow-Fuse threshold comparison, where NaN > threshold is false and would otherwise read as "under threshold" (AC-9).

MET-G1810.message: stage-funding command for {stage} carries a non-finite projected Series value {series}
MET-G1810.remedy: Attach a ProjectedConsequence.Series whose rendered values are all finite. A NaN/±Inf value would make the projected delta (last minus first) non-finite and, once enqueued, would poison Curve(education.attainment) with NaN/±Inf permanently; the whole series is finite-checked at the write boundary before the projection is enqueued (AC-9).

MET-G1900.remedy: data/refuse.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation (missing file, malformed JSON, a non-positive bin capacity, a negative waste rate, a stream-mix fraction outside [0,1], a contamination penalty outside [0,1], a compost conversion ratio outside (0,1], a negative vermin/incineration rate, a funding threshold outside [0,1], or a non-positive truck capacity/crews-per-truck). Fix the data file; every failure is registry-sourced, never a silent default substitution (AC-13).

MET-G1901.message: cell {cell} has an unknown or unregistered land-use type
MET-G1901.remedy: A bin-stock query or cell registration named a land-use type this package does not recognise (not residential/commercial/industrial), or a cell that was never registered and so has no land-use type. Register the cell first (RegisterCell), or fix the land-use value — never a silently-created zero-value bin-stock entry (AC-13).

MET-G1902.remedy: A round was scheduled (or a strike set) against a depot ID RegisterDepot never registered. Register the depot first, or fix the id — never a silently-created zero-value round (AC-13).

MET-G1903.message: round {round} is unknown or already completed
MET-G1903.remedy: OverrideRound (or AutoOptimise/ClearOverride/Round) was called on a round that is unknown or has already run. A completed round's history is never silently overridden (AC-14).

MET-G1904.remedy: SetContamination requires a fraction in [0,1]. A value below 0 or above 1 is rejected with this typed error, never silently clamped (AC-14).

MET-G1905.remedy: SetFunding requires a fraction in [0,1]. Rejected at this package's boundary before delegating to engine.services, never silently clamped (AC-14).

MET-G1906.message: disposal site {site} is unavailable (unknown, full, reclaimed, or wrong kind)
MET-G1906.remedy: General (or food) waste was routed to a site that is unknown, full, reclaimed, or not the right kind for that stream (a compost site cannot take general waste; only a landfill can be reclaimed). Route to a valid site instead — the tonnage is rejected rather than silently dropped (AC-8).

MET-G1907.message: RefuseAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G1907.remedy: Always use the *RefuseAPI pointer Load returned. Dereferencing-and-reassigning produces a second value with its own mutex but aliased maps, defeating the concurrency-safety invariant (SEC-020-class). If you need a second API, call Load again.

MET-G1908.remedy: The operation drives the registered outbound edges (engine.logistics/engine.services) before Wire injected them. Wire the dependencies before the first tick — an unwired call is rejected rather than silently treating a nil dependency as empty (GR#20).

MET-G1700.remedy: The intermodal container-transfer point refuses a non-positive tonnage, an unknown transport mode (sea/rail/road), a from==to no-op handoff, or a tonnage exceeding the intermodal modal cap (the smaller of the source and destination modes' per-movement max from data/freight.json). A malformed or over-cap transfer cannot satisfy engine.rail.md AC-3's tonnes-conservation contract; over-cap tonnage is rejected, never clamped.

MET-G1701.message: RailAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value, not the one NewRailAPI constructed
MET-G1701.remedy: Call methods on the *RailAPI returned by NewRailAPI, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's ledgers while holding an independent lock, so it is rejected before the lock is touched.

MET-G1702.remedy: data/freight.json's modalCaps could not be read (missing file or malformed JSON) or a mode is missing a positive maxTonnesPerMovement. NewRailAPI fails rather than returning a caps-less surface that would silently accept an over-cap intermodal transfer (GR#7/GR#15).

MET-G2000.remedy: The deep-sea terminal is permit-gated (feat.facilitypermits), milestone-gated by its data-driven tier milestone, and carries a day-one decommission liability (feat.decommission); an unwired seam, an intermodal transfer through an unregistered point, or a Build that is not a strict upgrade (a downgrade or repeat of an already-built tier) is refused. Wire the permit/decommission/rail seams, meet the milestone, and only ever build a strictly higher tier — no terminal state is mutated on a refused build.

MET-G2001.remedy: The port-tier ladder loaded from data/containerport.json holds cargo_port_small, container_terminal and deep_sea_terminal. Use one of those keys (or add the tier to the data file) rather than a silently-created zero-value tier.

MET-G2002.remedy: data/containerport.json could not be read or failed schema validation (a tier missing its key/name/disclosure, a non-positive berth count, a non-positive crane rate/operating hours/customs capacity, a non-positive ship tonnage, a negative jobs/milestone/cost figure, an unknown deepSeaTier key, or a port-tier ladder that is not strictly ascending — deep_sea_terminal must sort strictly above container_terminal on the (milestone, cost) key). Correct the data file — the ladder never falls back to a partial config, an inverted ordering, or a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G2100.message: data/leisure.json could not be read or failed schema validation: {cause}
MET-G2100.remedy: data/leisure.json must exist, be well-formed JSON, and pass schema validation (a positive version, a positive hoursPerWeek, a lifeStages entry for every life stage, an eventCrowd entry for every event kind, and a defaultPopulationTaste entry for every venue category). Correct the data file — the module never falls back to a partial config or a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G2101.remedy: A patronage/unmet-demand/leisure-fit query was issued for a citizen ID with no record in engine.citizens. Query a real citizen ID; the error is returned rather than a silently-zero-valued patronage record (AC-11).

MET-G2102.remedy: An unmet-demand or venue-mix query named a district (non-zero) that has no registered venues. Use 0 for the citywide aggregate, or query a district that actually holds venues (AC-11).

MET-G2103.message: event scheduled with a malformed or missing date/venue reference: {field}
MET-G2103.remedy: An event on the §42 calendar must carry a day-of-month in [0, 30) and a non-zero venue reference. A malformed or missing field is rejected at schedule time so a UI-promised payoff is never silently dropped (AC-12).

MET-G2104.remedy: A freshness/visit/refurbish/schedule operation named a venue ID that was never registered via OpenVenue. Register the venue first, or fix the reference.

MET-G2105.remedy: OpenVenue refuses a zero venue ID, a category outside the seven going-out categories (home is not a venue category), or a non-positive weekly capacity. Correct the venue before registering it.

MET-G2106.message: leisure operation {operation} requires dependency {dependency} to be wired
MET-G2106.remedy: Wire the missing dependency (citizens via SetCitizens, traffic via SetTraffic, wellbeing via SetWellbeing) before invoking the operation. The operation fails loudly rather than returning a fabricated figure.

MET-G2107.message: LeisureAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G2107.remedy: Call methods on the *LeisureAPI returned by New/Load, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's maps while holding an independent lock, so it is rejected before the lock is touched.

MET-G2108.remedy: LeisureFitAggregate/SetPopulationTaste received a distribution with a non-finite or negative entry, or one that sums to zero. Supply a normalised, non-negative distribution over the eight venue categories.

MET-G2109.remedy: A numeric input (e.g. overtime hours) was non-finite or negative. Supply a finite, non-negative value rather than relying on a silent clamp.

MET-G2200.message: data/wellbeing.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {cause}
MET-G2200.remedy: data/wellbeing.json must exist, be well-formed JSON, and pass schema validation (a positive version, baselines within [0,100], non-negative per-driver weights, a strictly-increasing age curve with at least two anchors, a commute threshold with the steeper-above shape, a rent-burden threshold in [0,1), and a positive unemployment cap). Correct the data file — the module never falls back to a partial config or a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G2201.message: attribution query supplied an out-of-domain driver input {field}={value}
MET-G2201.remedy: Every driver input has a documented domain (commute minutes >= 0, personality axes in [0,100], rent burden >= 0, fraction inputs in [0,1], satisfaction in [0,100]). Supply an in-domain value — the out-of-domain value is rejected, never silently clamped and folded into the wellbeing total (AC-13).

MET-G2202.message: attribution query supplied a non-finite driver input {field}={value}
MET-G2202.remedy: NaN/±Inf must never propagate into the conserved wellbeing sum. Fix the upstream source (a poisoned fixture, a division by zero, or an unguarded float) before it reaches this boundary (SEC-093).

MET-G2203.message: operation {operation} requires dependency {dependency} to be wired
MET-G2203.remedy: AttributeCitizen requires engine.season (the §9/§18 seasonal health wave is a mandatory physical component this module must source from engine.season, AC-10). Wire it via SetSeason before calling — its absence is a wiring error, not a degradable per-driver gap.

MET-G2204.message: WellbeingAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G2204.remedy: Call methods on the *WellbeingAPI returned by New/Load, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's mutex/source fields while holding an independent lock, so it is rejected before the lock is touched.

MET-G2205.remedy: A query was issued for a citizen ID with no record in the wired CitizensAPI. Query a real citizen ID; the error is returned rather than a silently-zero-valued attribution (AC-11).

MET-G2300.message: news generation referenced an entity that does not resolve to a name (entityId={entityId}, eventId={eventId}): {cause}
MET-G2300.remedy: The event's EntityID must resolve through the wired RoadNamer (the engine.roads naming seam). Wire the seam with SetRoadNamer before ingesting events that reference an entity, or ingest only events with an empty entity reference. The story is rejected — never a fabricated placeholder name and never a silently dropped story (AC-8).

MET-G2301.message: the embedded salience weight table could not be loaded or failed schema validation (field={field}, rule={rule}, cause={cause})
MET-G2301.remedy: The embedded salience.json must be valid JSON carrying a positive, finite weight for every §29 category (death|first|record|crisis|milestone) and a non-empty pending-tuning disclosure. Correct the embedded data file — the module never falls back to a silent default weight table (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G2302.message: LLM rewrite of event {eventId} altered an engine fact and was rejected; engine prose retained
MET-G2302.remedy: The optional LLM soft-layer produced prose that changed a name or number. The engine prose is published unchanged (AC-6/AC-7). The rejection is surfaced and logged (GR#17) so a misbehaving rewriter is visible, never silently absorbed.

MET-G2303.remedy: Ingest rejects an event that cannot become a well-formed story: a non-empty ID after trimming, a non-negative tick and magnitude, a known §29 category present in the salience weight table, and non-empty prose after trimming. Fix the event at its source (GR#1/GR#16).

MET-G2304.message: NewsAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G2304.remedy: Call methods on the *NewsAPI returned by New, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's mutex while holding an independent lock, so it is rejected before the lock is touched.

MET-G2305.message: the embedded fact-word list could not be loaded or failed schema validation (field={field}, rule={rule}, cause={cause})
MET-G2305.remedy: The embedded news-facts.json must be valid JSON carrying a non-empty fact-bearing token list (all lowercase letter words, no duplicates) and a non-empty pending-tuning disclosure. Correct the embedded data file — the FactLock fails closed (rejects every rewrite) rather than silently verifying against an empty fact-word set (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G2400.message: data/accelerator.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation from {dir}: {cause}
MET-G2400.remedy: Check that data/accelerator.json exists under the resolved data directory and passes schema validation (version present, positive peak multiplier, research multiplier above 1, non-negative health/FDI/prestige/threshold figures).

MET-G2401.message: particle-accelerator build rejected: the expert gate verdict is unmet at the current research output (threshold {threshold})
MET-G2401.remedy: Fund the education pipeline until engine.education's research output reaches data/accelerator.json's expertGateThreshold; money, milestones, and development points alone cannot satisfy the gate (the 'money alone cannot buy it' mechanic).

MET-G2402.remedy: Use the registered accelerator catalogue key (data/buildings.json's hadron_research_ring entry, which this module reconciles against in place). An out-of-taxonomy key is rejected rather than silently accepted.

MET-G2403.message: particle-accelerator build rejected: no valid facility permit is held for {key}

MET-G2500.message: data/pharmacampus.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {cause}

MET-G2502.message: pharma bid referenced an unavailable education-output term: {reason}

MET-G2503.message: won pharma campus could not emit graduate/research demand: {reason}

MET-G2505.message: won pharma campus could not route its export flow through the trade edge: {reason}

MET-G2800.message: data/airport.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {cause}
MET-G2800.remedy: data/airport.json must exist, be well-formed JSON, and pass schema validation (a positive version; a tier missing its key/name/disclosure; a non-positive runway/per-runway-rate/gate/per-gate-rate/reach-multiplier/freight-apron/contour-radius/noise-level/land-footprint figure; a negative jobs/cost/milestone figure; an unknown access tier or blight class; a reduced-throughput percentage outside (0,100); or a reach/access ladder that is not monotonic non-decreasing with at least one strict reach increase). Correct the data file — the module never falls back to a partial config or a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G2801.remedy: The airport is permit-gated (feat.facilitypermits), milestone-gated by its data-driven tier milestone, land-gated by its data-driven footprint, blight-gated through engine.mining’s BlightAPI registration, and its air-cargo arm must be wired to engine.freight. An unwired permit/blight/freight seam, a permit that is not granted, insufficient land, a non-positive air-cargo tonnage, or a Build that is not a strict upgrade is refused — no airport state is mutated on a refused build (AC-10).

MET-G2802.message: airport tier/component lookup failed — unknown tier key, or a component of an airport that has not been built
MET-G2802.remedy: The queried airport-tier key is not one of the loaded data/airport.json tiers, or a component was queried before any airport was built. Query an existing tier, or build the airport first — never a silently-created zero-value tier or a silently-zeroed component figure (AC-10).

MET-G2803.message: AirportAPI method called on a struct-copied *AirportAPI: {method}
MET-G2803.remedy: A struct-copied *AirportAPI aliases the original’s internal maps but gets its own zeroed mutex and keeps the original’s self pointer, so the copy is rejected before the mutex is ever touched (SEC-020 family).
