MET-G2700.message: CensusAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G2700.remedy: Call methods on the *CensusAPI returned by New/Load, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's mutex/tracked/history maps while holding an independent lock, so it is rejected before the lock is touched.

MET-G2701.remedy: Query the census for a bio or check-in record by a GUID that a tracked object actually carries. No zero-value bio/check-in is fabricated — the caller gets this error instead of a fabricated empty figure (AC-21).

MET-G2702.message: no aggregate or KPI with key {key}
MET-G2702.remedy: Resolve a Source drill-target or query a KPI by one of the census's documented aggregate keys. No zero-value aggregate is fabricated — the caller cannot mistake a fabricated 0 for a real empty figure (AC-21).

MET-G2703.message: data/census.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {cause}
MET-G2703.remedy: data/census.json must exist, be well-formed JSON, and pass schema validation (a positive version, a non-empty meta block, and every numeric entry carrying a finite value, a stated unit, and a non-empty disclosure comment; positive lifespan/retirement figures, happiness weights summing to 1.0, and in-range thresholds). Correct the data file — the module never falls back to a partial config or a silent default (GR#15/GR#7, AC-22).

MET-G2704.message: operation {operation} requires dependency {dependency} to be wired
MET-G2704.remedy: Wire the missing source (one of the seven consumed modules — citizens/education/crime/wellbeing/services/policies/finance) via its Wire* method before running the operation. The census fails closed rather than silently reporting a zero aggregate from an absent source (GR#1).

MET-G2705.message: education stage kind {stage} is outside the [0,7] census stage domain (citizen {citizen})
MET-G2705.remedy: An education source returned a stage kind the census does not model. The snapshot boundary rejects it (SEC-126) rather than indexing a fixed [numStages]int64 array out of range and panicking the observation pipeline; correct the source's stage data.

MET-G2706.message: object GUID {guid} is malformed or contradicts its declared kind/lifeSpan
MET-G2706.remedy: TrackObject was called with a GUID that fails the kind:numeric-id parse, or with a kind/lifeSpan that contradicts the GUID's prefix. Use a GUID built by the census constructors (citizenGUID/carGUID/houseGUID/chopperGUID) with its matching kind, and a whole-game life span for a citizen (SEC-127).

MET-G2707.remedy: A consumed module returned NaN/±Inf where the census stores a finite figure (crime rate, happiness, unfed fraction, or the education-policy coefficient). Rejected at the snapshot boundary so a non-finite value can never silently disable the regulator watchdog — NaN > threshold is false (SEC-130, GR#17).

MET-G2900.message: data/worklife.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {cause}
MET-G2900.remedy: data/worklife.json must exist, be well-formed JSON, and pass schema validation (a positive version, exactly the three documented pattern kinds — core-hours/shift/any-time — each once, every pattern's hoursPerDay in (0,24] and daysPerWeek in (0,7], a positive coverage span, a non-empty disclosure comment, a core-hours 0<=startHour<endHour<=24 window, shift rotations that contiguously tile the coverage span, and every working-week policy with positive hours, a finite wage coefficient >= 1, and a finite non-negative wellbeing weight). Correct the data file — the module never falls back to a partial config or a silent default (GR#15/GR#7, AC-15).

MET-G2901.remedy: A query referenced a pattern kind that is not one of the three documented kinds (core-hours / shift / any-time) carried in the loaded data. Use a registered kind; the error is returned rather than silently treating the worker as never-at-work (AC-14).

MET-G2902.remedy: An hours input (a per-hour demand, a working-week hour figure, or a policy effect's hours) was negative or exceeded the 24-hour day / 168-hour week. Rejected rather than silently clamped and folded into a coverage or hours figure (AC-14).

MET-G2903.remedy: An active working-week policy resolved to no known policy in the policy source. Rejected rather than silently falling back to the default week as if the policy were real (AC-14).

MET-G2904.message: WorkScheduleAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G2904.remedy: A *WorkScheduleAPI was copied by value, which would alias its mutex/source fields across two values. Call methods on the value returned by New/Load, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family).

MET-G2905.message: operation {operation} requires dependency {dependency} to be wired
MET-G2905.remedy: OverworkWellbeingInput was called before the engine.wellbeing seam was wired. Wire it via SetWellbeing before computing the overwork input; the module fails closed rather than silently skipping the push (AC-12).

MET-G2906.remedy: A wage coefficient or wellbeing weight crossing a module boundary was NaN or ±Inf, or a computed boundary value was non-finite. Rejected at the boundary rather than propagated into a wage or wellbeing figure (SEC-093).

MET-G3000.message: data/spaceport.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {cause}
MET-G3000.remedy: data/spaceport.json must exist, be well-formed JSON, carry a positive version and a non-empty catalogueAnchor, and give every numeric value a unit and a non-empty disclosure (AC-15). Correct the data file — the module never falls back to a partial config or a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G3001.message: spaceport catalogue anchor {anchor} does not resolve to exactly one data/buildings.json entry ({rule})
MET-G3001.remedy: The spaceport must resolve to exactly one catalogue entry (AC-1). A missing anchor or a second launch-site entry is a GR#3 violation; correct the anchor or the catalogue so exactly one entry matches, rather than silently defaulting.

MET-G3002.message: build command facility key {facilityKey} is outside the spaceport taxonomy (anchor {anchor})
MET-G3002.remedy: Submit a build command whose facilityKey equals the spaceport's catalogue anchor. Any other key is out-of-taxonomy and rejected before any state is touched (AC-10).

MET-G3003.message: expert gate unmet: education output {output} below the threshold {threshold}
MET-G3003.remedy: The shared expert gate (§8) gates the spaceport on engine.education's research output — money, milestones, and development points cannot substitute (AC-3). Fund education until the output reaches the data/spaceport.json threshold, then retry.

MET-G3004.message: no valid facility permit held for {facilityKey}
MET-G3004.remedy: A spaceport build is permit-gated via the facility-permit system (FEAT-053). Obtain a valid permit for the facility, then retry the build (AC-8).

MET-G3005.message: launch scheduled against an unbuilt or incomplete facility {facilityKey} ({state})
MET-G3005.remedy: Launches never fire before the multi-year build completes (AC-4). Complete the build (advance buildMonths months, one Tick each) before scheduling or projecting launches.

MET-G3006.message: a spaceport is already building or built ({anchor})
MET-G3006.remedy: The spaceport is a one-of-a-kind mega-facility (§MP). A second build command against an already-sited/building/built facility is rejected rather than silently double-building.

MET-G3007.message: SpaceportAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G3007.remedy: A copied *SpaceportAPI would alias its mutex across two values (SEC-020). Call methods on the value returned by New/Load, never a struct copy.

MET-G3008.message: operation {operation} requires seam {dependency} to be wired
MET-G3008.remedy: Wire the missing seam (education gate / permit gate / decommission liability / FDI draw / tourism draw) via its Set* method before running the operation. The spaceport fails closed rather than no-op-ing on an absent dependency (GR#1).

MET-G3009.remedy: Month indices are absolute and non-negative (0 = genesis). Pass a non-negative month to Tick.

MET-G3010.message: build command site coordinates ({siteX},{siteY}) must be non-negative
MET-G3010.remedy: The exclusion-contour centre must be a non-negative cell coordinate. Pass a valid site and retry (AC-10).

MET-G3100.message: data/fiscal.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {cause}
MET-G3100.remedy: data/fiscal.json must exist, be well-formed JSON, carry a positive version, and pass schema validation (a positive funding target, ordered zero/full curve anchors, a corruption threshold in (0,1], a positive childcare subsidy and second-earner wage, and an uplift fraction in [0,1]). Correct the data file — the module never falls back to a partial config or a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

An unknown category is rejected — never silently returned as a zero-value node that looks like a real, built producer (AC-10).

MET-G3102.message: FiscalAPI method {method} called on a copied value
MET-G3102.remedy: Hold the *FiscalAPI returned by New/Load; do not copy the struct. A copied value aliases its mutex and state across two values, so the copy guard rejects the call (SEC-020 family).

MET-G3103.remedy: Wire the missing dependency (engine.finance via SetFinance, engine.tax via SetTax) before the operation. The fiscal circuit fails closed rather than fabricating a figure on an absent dependency (GR#17).

MET-G3104.message: planning funding level {level} is outside [0,1] or non-finite
MET-G3104.remedy: SetPlanningFunding accepts a fraction in [0,1]. An out-of-range or non-finite level is rejected, never silently clamped (AC-5).

MET-G3105.remedy: Money and counts are never negative, and rates must be finite and non-negative. Reject the bad input rather than storing it (GR#16).

MET-G3106.remedy: The gross x rate intermediate exceeded int64, so the honest net/clawback figure cannot be computed. It is surfaced rather than returning a net that reads roughly equal to gross at a high rate (SEC-094 class).

MET-G3200.message: data/maintenance.json could not be read or failed schema validation
MET-G3200.remedy: data/maintenance.json must exist, be well-formed JSON, and pass schema validation (at least two classes, each with a positive engineer-days/year rate, a positive simulation-years lifetime, and a non-empty disclosure). Correct the data file - the module never falls back to a partial config or a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G3201.remedy: The named class key has no entry in data/maintenance.json. Use a resolvable class key (today engine.build zone types); the error is returned rather than a silently-zero-valued figure (AC-11).

MET-G3202.remedy: The named structure reference was never registered. Query a registered structure; the error is returned rather than a silently-zero-valued view (AC-11).

MET-G3203.remedy: A crew daily budget is an engineer-day figure and must be non-negative. Reject the bad budget rather than storing it (AC-11).

MET-G3204.remedy: Age advances by simulation month index only; a negative advance would drive an age negative. Reject rather than mutate (AC-11).

MET-G3205.remedy: The input is outside its documented domain (zero/duplicate structure id, non-positive job cost). Reject rather than silently accepting a no-op (AC-11).

MET-G3206.message: MaintenanceAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G3206.remedy: A *MaintenanceAPI is a mutex-bearing value; a struct copy would alias its state. Construct via New/Load and call methods on that value (SEC-020).

MET-G3300.message: engine.comms data file at {path} is invalid: {reason}
MET-G3300.remedy: data/comms.json must declare exactly the six §35 connectivity eras in order (telephone-exchange, dial-up, broadband-hub, fibre-backbone, cellular-masts, submarine-cable), each with the documented gate values, and a valid sectors/eCommerce/post/drain/fulfilment block. MET-G3301.message: CommsAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G3301.remedy: A *CommsAPI is a mutex-bearing value; a struct copy would alias its state and corrupt the copy guard. Construct via Load/LoadDefault and call methods on that value (SEC-020).

MET-G3302.message: era value {era} is outside the six-era connectivity ladder
MET-G3302.remedy: Only the six §35 eras (telephone exchange through submarine cable) are valid inputs to a capability-gate query or an era advance. Reject an out-of-enum era rather than silently creating a zero-value era state (AC-10).

MET-G3303.message: era advance to {target} skips an intermediate era (current {current})
MET-G3303.remedy: The six-era ladder is monotonic and must be advanced one step at a time — a single advance may not skip an intermediate era (AC-2). Advance through each intermediate era first.

MET-G3304.message: era {target} is not unlocked (milestone tier {tier} not reached)
MET-G3304.remedy: This era's §4 milestone tier has not been reached (or no milestone gate is wired — fail closed). Reach the tier via the unlock-tree system, or wire the gate, before advancing.

MET-G3305.message: fulfilment-centre registration has no firm reference (engine.firms not wired)
MET-G3305.remedy: A fulfilment centre must register as a real firm through engine.firms (AC-7). Wire engine.firms via SetFirms before registering a fulfilment centre.

MET-G3306.message: delivery movement has no logistics reference (engine.logistics not wired)
MET-G3306.remedy: Fulfilment-centre and last-mile-depot delivery trips are real engine.logistics movements (AC-8). Wire engine.logistics via SetLogistics before resolving deliveries.

MET-G3307.message: postal service has no services reference (engine.services not wired)
MET-G3307.remedy: The sorting office and parcel hub draw from the generic §10 service pool (US-5). Wire engine.services via SetServices before registering postal infrastructure.

MET-G3308.message: input {field} = {value} is outside its documented domain
MET-G3308.remedy: Wealth and counterplay offset are fractions in [0,1] (0-100%); letter/parcel volume inputs are non-negative. Reject an out-of-domain input rather than silently clamping (AC-11).

MET-G3309.remedy: A NaN or ±Inf value reached a numeric boundary. Reject it before any ordered range check, so a non-finite value can never slip through a range gate (SEC-093).

MET-G3310.message: sector {sector} is outside the documented sector buckets
MET-G3310.remedy: Remote-work share is sector-dependent (AC-4); only the five documented sector buckets (none/primary/secondary/tertiary/public) carry a remote-work affinity. Pass a valid sector.

MET-G3311.remedy: A fulfilment-centre query or e-commerce-infrastructure precondition found no registered fulfilment centre. Register one via RegisterFulfilmentCentre first.

MET-G3400.remedy: data/capexport.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation (missing file, malformed JSON, a non-positive rate, an empty id/label/unit, a non-finite projection growth rate, or a duplicate line id). Fix the data file; every failure is registry-sourced, never a silent default substitution (AC-5).

MET-G3401.remedy: A query or command named an ExportableService id that is not one of the catalogue's registered lines. Use one of the ten §36 in-scope lines (see data/capexport.json); never a zero-value surplus book silently returned for a line that does not exist (AC-5).

MET-G3402.remedy: IssueContract was asked to sell more than the line's exportable slack (capacity − internal demand − already committed). Reduce the quantity or free capacity; the contract is rejected at issue time, never a silently-oversold contract that only fails later at the crossing (AC-8).

MET-G3403.remedy: An operation addressed a contract id that was never issued, is already cancelled, or whose term has ended. Reject rather than silently no-op or return a zero-valued contract (AC-9).

MET-G3404.remedy: An operation that needs a wired dependency (engine.services / engine.finance / engine.projections) was invoked before that dependency was wired. Wire it via SetServices/SetFinance/SetProjections; fail loudly rather than fabricating a figure (GR#17).

MET-G3405.message: method {method} called on a struct-copied CapExportAPI
MET-G3405.remedy: A CapExportAPI method was called on a struct-copied value. A copied *CapExportAPI would alias its mutex/maps across two values, so the copy guard rejects the call (SEC-020).

MET-G3406.remedy: IssueContract/AccrueRevenue/SetMonth/SetDemandGrowth was handed an out-of-domain input — a non-positive quantity/term/rate, a negative rate, a non-monotonic month, or a non-finite quantity. Reject rather than silently clamp (GR#16).

MET-G3407.remedy: CutInternalService was invoked for a line whose internal demand has not crossed its committed capacity — there is no shortfall to cut, so the choice is not offered. Check Crossing first; never a cut that silently reduces coverage by zero (AC-3).

MET-G3408.message: no engine.services instance bound for line {line}
MET-G3408.remedy: A surplus/coverage query addressed an exportable line with no engine.services instance bound via BindServiceLine. Bind one first; capacity/demand is always sourced through ServicesAPI, never invented (GR#20).

MET-G3500.message: checkpoint Manager method called on a struct-copied value, not the one NewManager constructed
MET-G3500.remedy: Always use the *Manager pointer NewManager returned; a struct copy gets its own independent mu while aliasing the same underlying save.Manager (SEC-020-class). Construct a second independent Manager via NewManager if needed.

MET-G3501.message: checkpoint identifier "{id}" is not a valid single path component: {cause}
MET-G3501.remedy: A checkpoint ID becomes a bundle directory name under manual/, so it must pass serialize.ValidateShardName (no path separators, "..", ".", drive markers, or trailing dot/space). Choose a plain identifier.

MET-G3502.message: checkpoint operation rejected: another checkpoint operation is already in flight on the same Manager
MET-G3502.remedy: CreateCheckpoint/Revert are serialised per Manager; wait for the in-flight operation to complete (or fail) before retrying, mirroring feat.saveux's single-save-in-flight guard.

MET-G3503.message: writing checkpoint-meta.json lineage sidecar for "{dir}" failed: {cause}
MET-G3503.remedy: The just-saved bundle is rolled back (removed) so no half-recorded checkpoint is left discoverable. Check filesystem permissions/free space and retry.

MET-G3504.remedy: The just-created bundle is rolled back so the on-disk fork tree never disagrees with the recorded active head. Check filesystem permissions/free space and retry.

MET-G3505.remedy: The pointer file exists but is malformed. Restore it from a backup or remove it to reset the active-head tracking (Lineage degrades to 'no active head'; CurrentID surfaces this error).

MET-G3506.message: checkpoint parent "{parent}" does not name an existing checkpoint
MET-G3506.remedy: Lineage is recorded explicitly (AC-4) and must not dangle. Create the parent checkpoint first, or pass an empty parent to create a root checkpoint.

MET-G3507.message: revert target "{target}" is not a checkpoint (no checkpoint-meta.json)
MET-G3507.remedy: Revert requires a checkpoint bundle. Ensure the target was created by CreateCheckpoint/Revert (a regular manual save is not a checkpoint).

MET-G3508.remedy: A filesystem-level failure listing the manual/ checkpoint subdirectory (distinct from a single malformed bundle, which Lineage skips per-entry). Check filesystem permissions and the root path.

MET-G3509.message: pruning failed partway; the retained set was left unchanged: {cause}
MET-G3509.remedy: Pruning's rename phase failed and every already-staged branch was renamed back (AC-9). Check filesystem permissions/free space; the extra abandoned branches will be retried on the next prune.

MET-G3510.message: invalid fork-retention configuration: value {value} is negative
MET-G3510.remedy: SetMaxRetainedForks requires a non-negative N. Pass 0 to retain no abandoned branches, or MaxRetainedForks for the default.

MET-G3511.message: checkpoint name "{name}" already occupies the manual/ namespace (an existing checkpoint or manual save)
MET-G3511.remedy: The manual/ namespace is shared with feat.saveux's SaveManual. Re-creating the name would save-over the prior bundle (destroying player data) and, for a checkpoint, could form a lineage cycle. Choose a new name, or Load/Revert the existing checkpoint / save instead.

MET-G3512.message: fork-name sequence exhausted while deriving a fork off "{target}"
MET-G3512.remedy: The persisted monotonic fork counter saturated (int64 max) while skipping past colliding checkpoint names. Unreachable in normal play; if seen, the checkpoint-head pointer was hand-edited — restore it from a backup.

MET-G3513.message: revert failed and could not restore the prior active head "{priorHead}" (restore error: {restoreCause}; original error: {originalCause})
MET-G3513.remedy: The revert's fork-save or head-write failed after the target had already been loaded into the live participants, and reloading the prior head to undo it also failed. Live state is left reverted while CurrentID is unchanged; investigate the restore error and reload the prior head manually.

MET-G3514.message: checkpoint name "{name}" is too long ({length} bytes; limit {max}) — a longer name would make its derived fork name exceed the manual-save name limit and become permanently unrevertible
MET-G3514.remedy: Checkpoint names are bounded to reserve the ".fork<seq>" suffix budget so every created checkpoint stays revertible at any fork sequence. Shorten the name to maxCheckpointNameLen bytes or fewer.

MET-G3515.message: cannot revert to "{target}": the derived fork name "{forkName}" is {length} bytes, over the manual-save name limit {max} — a fork-of-fork chain has grown the name past what a further revert could name
MET-G3515.remedy: Revert derives "<target>.fork<seq>", and each fork is itself a valid revert target, so a chain of reverts grows the name by ".fork<seq>" per level. This checkpoint cannot be reverted again because the next fork's name would exceed the 255-byte manual-save limit; revert to an earlier, shorter-named checkpoint instead. The rejection happens before any state is loaded, so live state is untouched.

MET-G3600.message: data/social.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation (dir {dir}): {cause}
MET-G3600.remedy: Check that data/social.json exists at the resolved data directory, is well-formed JSON, has a positive "version", carries finite non-negative caseload rates, a non-negative hostel/foster capacity and carers figure, and an interventionHarmThreshold in [0,1]. The social-services balance set never falls back to a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G3601.message: social-services category {category} is not one of the five registered provision categories
MET-G3601.remedy: Use one of the five §40 categories (family-support, homelessness, disability-carers, fostering, addiction). An unknown category is rejected rather than silently creating a zero-value case (AC-13).

MET-G3602.message: case {case} is not in the social-services case ledger
MET-G3602.remedy: Pass a CaseID minted by this module (AdvanceMonth, InjectCrisis, RecordChildProtectionIntervention, or EscalateCase). An unknown id is rejected rather than silently creating a zero-value case record (AC-13).

MET-G3603.message: funding level {level} for category {category} is outside [0,1]
MET-G3603.remedy: Funding levels are fractions in [0,1]. An out-of-domain level is rejected rather than silently clamped.

MET-G3604.message: escalation destination {destination} is not a registered social-services category
MET-G3604.remedy: EscalateCase requires a destination category that exists (AC-14). An escalation is a close-plus-reopen pair, so a phantom destination would unbalance the case-accounting identity.

MET-G3605.message: case {case} cannot be closed: already closed with status {status}
MET-G3605.remedy: A case can only be resolved/escalated/lost-to-follow-up once (AC-14). A double close is rejected rather than silently drifting the accounting identity.

MET-G3606.message: funding cut for category {category} with FuseYears {fuseYears} lacks a projected-consequence payload
MET-G3606.remedy: A Slow-Fuse funding cut (FuseYears above the A5 threshold) must carry a non-empty projected Series (AC-10). This module rejects it before it reaches engine.projections.

MET-G3607.message: funding cut for category {category} carried a non-finite or non-positive FuseYears {fuseYears}
MET-G3607.remedy: FuseYears must be a finite positive number. A degenerate tag is rejected so it can never be misread as under-threshold by a float comparison (AC-10).

MET-G3608.message: SocialAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G3608.remedy: A *SocialAPI is a mutex-bearing value; a struct copy would alias its state. Construct via New/Load and call methods on that value (SEC-020).

MET-G3609.message: SocialAPI operation {operation} needs dependency {dependency}, which is not wired
MET-G3609.remedy: Wire the dependency via SetCitizens/SetServices/SetFamilyStressSource/SetProjections before the operation. A missing dependency fails loudly rather than no-op-ing.

MET-G3610.message: projected-consequence series for category {category} contains a non-finite value
MET-G3610.remedy: The projected Series must contain only finite values; a NaN/±Inf would poison the projections curve, so it is rejected at the write boundary (GR#16).

MET-G3612.message: case {case} cannot be closed in month {month}: it opened in month {openedMonth}
MET-G3612.remedy: Pass a month at or after the case's OpenedMonth. A back-dated closure would record a Resolved/Escalated/LostToFollowUp event in a month with no matching Opened, driving the AC-11 conservation identity negative (GR#21).

MET-G3613.message: caseload driver input {field} = {value} is outside its documented domain {domain}
MET-G3613.remedy: Pass driver inputs within their documented domains: Deprivation and NightlifeDensity in [0,1], CrowdingStress and FinancialStress >= 0 (finite), and UnemploymentMonths >= 0. An out-of-domain value is rejected rather than producing an unbounded case-proposal count (SEC-181 resource-exhaustion).

MET-G3614.message: caseload proposal count {proposals} exceeds the per-month resource ceiling {max}
MET-G3614.remedy: The per-month (or per-crisis-event) case-proposal count is bounded by the resource ceiling maxCaseloadProposalsPerMonth, mirroring engine.core's MaxAdvanceTicksPerCall. A driver magnitude or config rate whose product with the data rates would allocate more cases than the ceiling is rejected before any allocation — it is a resource bound on the COUNT, not a balance bound on the driver, so a legitimate balance pass never reaches it (SEC-195).

MET-G3615.message: projected-consequence series carries {points} points, over the resource ceiling {max}
MET-G3615.remedy: The projected-consequence Series a funding cut carries is bounded by the resource ceiling maxProjectionSeriesPoints, mirroring maxCaseloadProposalsPerMonth. A series over the ceiling is rejected at the write boundary before any O(n) scan or allocation runs over it — it is a resource bound on the LENGTH, not a balance bound on the series values, so a legitimate slow-fuse consequence (a handful of months to a century) never reaches it (SEC-202).

MET-G3700.message: data/coastal.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation (field={field}, rule={rule}, path={path}, cause={cause})
MET-G3700.remedy: Check that data/coastal.json exists at the resolved data directory, is well-formed JSON, has a positive "version", finite non-negative frequency multipliers, a positive caseworker throughput, a finite grant rate in [0,1], and finite non-negative policy gain/cost figures. The coastal balance set never falls back to a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G3701.message: CoastalAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G3701.remedy: Call methods on the *CoastalAPI returned by New/Load, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's mutex while holding an independent lock, so it is rejected before the lock is touched.

MET-G3702.message: pipeline-stage query referenced unknown case ID {case}
MET-G3702.remedy: Case IDs are minted only by the scheduled Advance path (never a caller-invented ID, GR#20). An ID outside the recorded case set is rejected with this code rather than returning a fabricated zero-value stage (AC-13).

MET-G3703.message: policy coefficient {field} set to {value}, outside its documented domain
MET-G3703.remedy: The three policy sliders (processing funding, housing approach, integration investment) accept finite values in [0,1] only. An out-of-domain value is rejected rather than silently clamped, so a slider can never be set to a value the balance curves do not define (AC-13).

MET-G3704.message: arrival scheduled against cell ({x},{y}) which is not classified as shore
MET-G3704.remedy: Small-boat arrivals are placed only on cells the shore source classifies as shore (§30/§2.1). A drawn cell that fails the shore classification is rejected before any event is placed — never silently relocated to an arbitrary land cell (AC-14).

MET-G3705.message: dependency {dependency} required for operation {operation} is not wired
MET-G3705.remedy: Wire the outbound dependency (engine.citizens for granted-citizen creation, engine.services for rescue capacity, engine.news for factual reporting) via the matching Set* method before the operation that needs it. The operation fails closed rather than fabricating a result (GR#17).

MET-G3706.message: a NaN or ±Inf value reached the {field} boundary
MET-G3706.remedy: Reject the non-finite input before any ordered range check or arithmetic, so NaN/±Inf never leaks into stored case/cost state (GR#16/SEC-093).

MET-G3707.message: numeric input {field} = {value} outside its documented range
MET-G3707.remedy: Pass the input within its documented domain (e.g. month >= 0). An out-of-range value is rejected rather than silently clamped (GR#16).

MET-G3708.message: era/milestone tier {tier} outside the documented 0..13 ladder
MET-G3708.remedy: The arrival-frequency era multiplier table is indexed by the §4 milestone tier (0..13). A tier outside that ladder is rejected rather than indexing out of bounds or wrapping (AC-3/GR#16).

MET-G3709.message: season index {season} outside the documented 0..3 ladder
MET-G3709.remedy: The arrival-frequency season multiplier table is indexed by the four §27 seasons (0..3). A season index outside that ladder is rejected rather than indexing out of bounds (AC-3/GR#16).

MET-G3710.message: no shore source wired; arrival generation requires shore-cell membership
MET-G3710.remedy: Wire the shore-cell membership source via SetShore before Advance. Without it the module cannot know which cells are shore (§30/§2.1), so arrival generation fails closed rather than placing events on invented cells (AC-14).

MET-G3800.message: data/defence.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation (field={field}, rule={rule}, cause={cause})
MET-G3800.remedy: Check that data/defence.json exists at the resolved data directory, is well-formed JSON, has a positive "version", at least one competitive grant pot with finite in-[0,1] win-probability anchors, a positive formula-support threshold/amount, at least one mandate with a positive population threshold and at least two compliant choices, and a facility table covering every referenced facility type. The defence balance set never falls back to a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G3801.message: DefenceAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G3801.remedy: Call methods on the *DefenceAPI returned by New/Load, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's mutex while holding an independent lock, so it is rejected before the lock is touched.

MET-G3802.message: grant bid named an undeclared pot {pot}
MET-G3802.remedy: A grant bid must name one of data/defence.json's competitive pots (transport/regeneration/culture). An unknown pot is rejected loudly rather than silently accepted as a no-op a caller could mistake for a bid (AC-11).

MET-G3803.message: facility-siting command named an ineligible cell {site} (cause={cause})
MET-G3803.remedy: A facility site must fall inside the world grid and pass engine.build's ownership gate. An out-of-bounds or unowned cell is rejected before any facility is recorded — never a silently-accepted no-op (AC-11).

MET-G3804.remedy: A mandate can be accepted or refused exactly once. A second response is rejected rather than silently overwriting the first decision (AC-12).

MET-G3805.remedy: Mandate IDs come only from data/defence.json's mandate events (GR#20). An ID outside that set is rejected rather than fabricating a response for a mandate that was never issued (AC-11).

MET-G3806.message: mandate {mandate} choice {choice} is not one of the compliant choices
MET-G3806.remedy: A mandate's compliant choices are exactly those data/defence.json lists for it (AC-5). An out-of-set choice is rejected rather than auto-mapped to a default — the player's decision must be a real, recorded choice within compliance.

MET-G3807.message: grant bid rejected because a mandate refusal is in effect
MET-G3807.remedy: Refusing a mandate revokes central-grant access (AC-6) — the priced cost of the libertarian-city path. This refusal-specific rejection is distinct from an undeclared-pot or bad-bid rejection so a caller can tell the two apart.

MET-G3808.message: dependency {dependency} required for operation {operation} is not wired
MET-G3808.remedy: Wire the outbound dependency (engine.build for siting, engine.finance for compensation/grants, engine.citizens for personnel settlement) via the matching Set* method before the operation that needs it. The operation fails closed rather than fabricating a result (GR#17).

MET-G3809.message: numeric input {field} = {value} outside its documented domain
MET-G3809.remedy: Pass the input within its documented domain (e.g. month >= 0, match funding >= 0, planning quality in [0,1], wage-bill factor in [0,1]). An out-of-domain value is rejected rather than silently clamped (GR#16).

MET-G3810.message: facility query referenced an unknown or closed facility {facility}
MET-G3810.remedy: Facility IDs are minted only when a mandate is accepted (GR#20). A payroll/procurement/closure query against an ID outside the built-facility set is rejected rather than returning a fabricated zero-value figure (AC-9/AC-11).

MET-G3900.message: data/roads.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation (field={field}, reason={reason}, cause={cause})
MET-G3900.remedy: Check that data/roads.json exists at the resolved data directory, is well-formed JSON, has a positive "version", and declares exactly the eleven §51 class rungs in canonical order with positive lane counts, positive speed limits within speedMin..speedMax, positive widths, and valid maintenance/upgrade/roadworks/naming blocks. The roads balance set never falls back to a silent default (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G3901.message: RoadsAPI method {method} called on a struct-copied value
MET-G3901.remedy: Call methods on the *RoadsAPI returned by Load, never a struct copy of it (SEC-020 family). A copied value aliases the original's mutex while holding an independent lock, so it is rejected before the lock is touched.

MET-G3902.remedy: Road IDs are minted only by AddRoad. An upgrade/roadworks/query against an ID outside the added-road set is rejected rather than returning a fabricated zero-value road (AC-12).

MET-G3903.remedy: Register nodes via AddNode before referencing them from AddRoad. An edge referencing an unregistered endpoint is rejected rather than fabricating a node position.

MET-G3904.message: road class {class} is not one of the eleven §51 rungs
MET-G3904.remedy: Pass one of the eleven RoadClass values (alley through motorway). A class outside the ladder is rejected rather than silently mapped to a default (AC-3/AC-12).

MET-G3905.message: upgrade target rejected by the compatibility rule
MET-G3905.remedy: Check the documented compatibility rule in internal/engine/roads/doc.go. Under the provisional any-to-any rule every distinct valid class is compatible, so this code is reserved for the step-through-adjacent alternative if Aaron rules it — the rule is documented, never silently chosen.

MET-G3906.message: widening road {road} to {target} would overlap {count} occupied cell(s), first at {cell}
MET-G3906.remedy: Widening into a zoned or structured cell requires purchase/demolition first (AC-5). Clear the obstructing cell via the owning module (engine.build/world) and retry the upgrade; the upgrade is rejected rather than silently demolishing (GR#16).

MET-G3907.message: widening footprint check requires engine.world but none is wired
MET-G3907.remedy: Wire engine.world via SetWorld before applying a widening upgrade. The check fails closed rather than fabricating a footprint-occupancy answer (GR#17).

MET-G3908.remedy: Phases must be non-empty, time-ordered and non-overlapping, each with a non-negative start month, a positive duration, and an OpenLanes count in [0, steady-state lanes]; a WindowSummer schedule must start phases in calendar summer months (AC-6/AC-17).

MET-G3909.message: object kind {kind} is not a known §20 kind
MET-G3909.remedy: Pass one of the five ObjectKind values (road, civic building, infrastructure, district, transit). An unknown kind is rejected rather than silently returning an empty name (AC-13).

MET-G3910.message: speed limit {kph} for road {road} outside its class bounds [{min},{max}]
MET-G3910.remedy: Set the speed limit within the road class's speedMin..speedMax range (AC-2). An out-of-bounds value is rejected rather than silently clamped (GR#16).

MET-G3911.message: Advance target month {target} is before the current month {now}
MET-G3911.remedy: Simulation time must not run backwards. Advance only to a month at or after the current one (AC-17).

MET-G3912.remedy: Pass the input within its documented domain (a non-zero RoadID/NodeID, a non-negative repair amount, a non-empty rename, NameRoad for road naming). An out-of-domain value is rejected rather than silently clamped (GR#16).

MET-G3913.message: data/naming_corpus.json could not be loaded or validated (cause={cause})
MET-G3913.remedy: Check that data/naming_corpus.json exists at the resolved data directory and passes foundation.data's validation (non-empty distinct place names and a non-empty suffix list per road class). The naming service fails loudly rather than shipping an empty or placeholder name (AC-13).

MET-G3914.message: node {node} cannot be moved: it is referenced by a road
MET-G3914.remedy: A node already referenced by a road's start/end keeps its registered position. Re-registering it at a different position would desync the road's stored footprint from its endpoints (SEC-236); register the new position under a fresh NodeID instead.

MET-F900.message: T0-critical command {kind} could not be enqueued: the T0 queue has no disk fallback (must never be queued past the current tick) and its in-memory buffer is full
MET-F900.remedy: A full T0 buffer means the tick driver is not draining the queue (call QueuedTransport.Drain) fast enough, or T0MemCap is set too low for the burst. This is a registry error, never a silent drop, per GR#17/proposal section 4 -- the caller must retry or the tick driver must catch up before the command is lost for good.

MET-F901.message: T1-batchable command {kind} could not be spilled to its disk overflow segment (seq {seq}): {cause}
MET-F901.remedy: The atomic staging-write-then-rename to the T1 segment directory failed (disk full, permissions, or another filesystem error) -- the command was never queued at all, so per GR#17 this surfaces as a registry error rather than a silent drop. Free disk space / fix permissions under the configured overflow root and retry.

MET-F902.message: T1 disk overflow segment (seq {seq}) could not be read back or decoded during drain: {cause}
MET-F902.remedy: A promoted segment file failed protocol.DecodeCommand -- it is treated as corrupt/torn and NEVER surfaced as a valid command (mirrors internal/engine/save's validate-then-rename philosophy: a file only reaches its final path once fully written, so a decode failure here means something outside this package's own atomic writer touched the segment). Investigate what wrote or modified the file at that path; the drain halts rather than silently skipping or fabricating a command.

MET-F903.message: could not create the T1 overflow segment directory or its staging subdirectory under {root}: {cause}
MET-F903.remedy: os.MkdirAll failed for the configured disk overflow root (or its .spill-staging subdirectory) -- check the path is valid and writable. No command was queued as a result of this failure.

MET-F904.message: QueuedTransport method {method} was called on a struct copy of the value NewQueuedTransport returned
MET-F904.remedy: Always use the *QueuedTransport pointer NewQueuedTransport returned -- do not dereference-and-reassign it or pass it by value. A copy shares the aliased tier queues/inner transport but has its own independent mutexes, which is exactly the SEC-020-class hazard InProcTransport/Engine/Registry/Store/Screen/save.Manager's own checkNotCopied guards exist to reject before any lock is ever touched.

MET-F905.message: connection retry counter exceeded its configured cap ({maxRetries}) without op ever succeeding
MET-F905.remedy: Connection.Attempt's retry counter exceeded its configured cap without succeeding. The caller must explicitly call Reconnect to move past this state; Attempt never auto-escalates to reconnect on its own.

MET-F906.message: Connection.Reconnect's name-lookup, re-authentication, or post-reconnect catch-up drain failed
MET-F906.remedy: The connection falls back to StateRetrying (with its retry counter incremented) rather than being left in StateReconnecting/StateCatchingUp indefinitely -- a stuck non-terminal state would be a silent hang, not a registry error.

MET-F907.message: a *Connection method was called on a struct copy of the value NewConnection returned
MET-F907.remedy: Always use the *Connection pointer NewConnection returned -- do not dereference-and-reassign it or pass it by value. A copy shares the aliased fields but has its own independent mutexes, which is exactly the SEC-020-class hazard checkNotCopied guards exist to reject before any lock is ever touched.

MET-F908.message: Recover could not read the active checkpoint's head pointer or could not load its bundle back into the supplied participants
MET-F908.remedy: A crash-recovery attempt that cannot even establish its base state must fail loudly, never silently fall back to start from empty world. Check that the checkpoint directory and manager are correctly configured and present.

MET-F909.message: a WAL entry (or the WAL-CURRENT slot pointer) that DOES exist at its final path could not be listed, read, or decoded
MET-F909.remedy: A promoted WAL entry failed to read or decode -- it is treated as corrupt and never surfaced as a valid command. Investigate what wrote or modified the file at that path; recovery halts rather than silently skipping or fabricating a command. A torn/never-promoted tail write is NOT this error -- it is simply absent from the WAL slot's directory listing.

MET-F910.message: a caller-supplied apply function returned an error while replaying a decoded command from the WAL: {cause}
MET-F910.remedy: Recovery halts immediately rather than continuing past a failed apply to prevent producing a rebuilt state that is not byte-identical to the pre-crash state, defeating determinism (GR#21).

MET-F911.message: could not create a WAL slot directory or its staging subdirectory under {root}: {cause}
MET-F911.remedy: os.MkdirAll failed for the configured WAL slot root (or its .wal-staging subdirectory) -- check the path is valid and writable. No entry was appended and no prune progressed as a result.

MET-F912.message: WAL entry (seq {seq}) or the WAL-CURRENT pointer could not be durably written: {cause}
MET-F912.remedy: The atomic staging-write-then-rename to the WAL slot directory (or to the WAL-CURRENT pointer file) failed (disk full, permissions, or another filesystem error). The entry was never durably logged -- a command whose Append call returns this error MUST NOT be applied, or the commit-before-apply race this package exists to close reoccurs on the WAL's own persistence path.

MET-F913.message: WAL prune could not finish rebuilding the inactive slot or flip the WAL-CURRENT pointer: {cause}
MET-F913.remedy: The WAL-CURRENT pointer is only ever flipped after every retained entry is durably written to the rebuilt slot, so this failure always leaves the previously active slot still active and fully intact -- no data was lost, only the disk space this prune would have reclaimed. Free disk space / fix permissions and retry the prune on the next checkpoint.

MET-F914.message: a *WAL method was called on a struct copy of the value NewWAL returned
MET-F914.remedy: Always use the *WAL pointer NewWAL returned -- do not dereference-and-reassign it or pass it by value. A copy shares the aliased root/slot fields but has its own independent mutex, which is exactly the SEC-020-class hazard checkNotCopied guards exist to reject before any lock is ever touched.

MET-F915.message: a *Registry method was called on a struct copy of the value NewRegistry returned
MET-F915.remedy: Always use the *Registry pointer NewRegistry returned -- do not dereference-and-reassign it or pass it by value. A copy shares the aliased entries map but has its own independent mutex, which is exactly the SEC-020-class hazard checkNotCopied guards exist to reject before any lock is ever touched.

MET-F916.message: an *IntegrationMetrics method was called on a struct copy of the value Registry.Register returned
MET-F916.remedy: Always use the *IntegrationMetrics pointer Registry.Register returned -- do not dereference-and-reassign it or pass it by value. Same SEC-020-class copy-identity hazard as MET-F915, one level down.

MET-F917.message: ServeMetrics was called with no debug gate configured, or the configured gate denied the request
MET-F917.remedy: The monitoring dashboard's HTTP surface is debug-gated and fails closed by default -- wire an explicit Gate (mirroring engine.core's Speed8xGate / feat.devmode's debug.State.IsOn) before calling ServeMetrics; it must never start listening on a build/run where the composition root has not explicitly enabled it.

MET-F918.message: ServeMetrics was asked to bind an address that is not localhost-only: {addr}
MET-F918.remedy: The monitoring dashboard must never be reachable off-box. Pass an address whose host is 127.0.0.1, localhost, or ::1 (never a bare :port, which binds every interface).

MET-F919.message: net.Listen failed for the monitoring dashboard's (already validated localhost-only) address: {cause}
MET-F919.remedy: Check that the configured port is free and the process has permission to bind it; retry with a different Addr if the default port is already in use.

MET-G4000.message: data/policies.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {cause}
MET-G4000.remedy: Check that data/policies.json exists under the resolved data directory and passes engine.policies' schema validation (positive version; non-empty meta.combination naming the supported rule 'multiplicative'; positive meta.previewDrift tolerance and checkpoint cadence; every entry with a non-empty key/name/category/disclosure, one of the three scope kinds citywide/district/road, at least one coefficient move with a finite delta, and conflict references that all resolve to real policy keys). engine.policies never falls back to a partial or default-substituted library (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-G4001.remedy: The referenced policy key is not one of the entries loaded from data/policies.json. Use Policies() to enumerate the library, or add the entry to the data file.

MET-G4002.message: policy {policy} is already active in an identical scope ({scope})
MET-G4002.remedy: Enact in a different scope, or repeal the existing enactment first. engine.policies rejects an identical-scope re-enactment rather than silently no-op'ing (AC-13).

MET-G4003.message: scope resolution failed: unknown or malformed scope {scope}
MET-G4003.remedy: A scope named a DistrictID or road that is not registered, or a malformed scope (e.g. a citywide scope carrying a district ID). Create the district (CreateDistrict) or register the road (RegisterRoad) before resolving scope against it. Never a resolved-to-empty-set false success (AC-13).

MET-G4004.remedy: The district ID is not registered. Create it via CreateDistrict before querying or renaming it.

MET-G4005.remedy: The road ID is not registered. Register it via RegisterRoad before resolving a road scope against it.

MET-G4006.remedy: The enactment ID is not active. Enactments are created by Enact and removed by Repeal; check the ID against the current active set.

MET-G4007.message: scope mismatch for policy {policy}: declared {declared}, given {given}
MET-G4007.remedy: The concrete scope target's kind does not match the policy's declared scope kind. Enact/resolve a citywide policy with a citywide scope, a district policy with a district scope, and a road policy with a road scope.

MET-G4008.remedy: A coefficient delta was NaN or ±Inf. Fix the offending entry in data/policies.json — a non-finite delta would poison the combination and projection arithmetic (GR#16).

MET-G4009.remedy: Wire engine.finance via SetFinance before enacting a policy with a non-zero cost or advancing the tick past an active policy's recurring opex. engine.policies never silently skips a monetary posting (GR#17).

MET-G4010.remedy: Wire engine.projections via SetProjections before previewing or enacting a policy. The preview and the enactment both feed the shared curve machinery; an unwired projections dependency is a fail-closed error, never a silently-skipped model update (GR#17).

MET-G4011.remedy: Wire engine.tax via SetTax before enacting a policy that carries a data-declared tax coefficient move. engine.policies routes tax moves through TaxAPI rather than reimplementing tax mechanics (GR#3/GR#20).

MET-G4012.message: PoliciesAPI method {method} was called on a struct copy of the value NewPoliciesAPI/Load returned
MET-G4012.remedy: Always use the *PoliciesAPI pointer NewPoliciesAPI/Load returned -- do not dereference-and-reassign it or pass it by value. A copy shares the aliased library/district/active maps but has its own independent mutexes, the SEC-020-class hazard every Register-shaped module in this codebase rejects before any lock is touched.

MET-G4013.message: simulation month regression: requested month {month} is before the current month {current}
MET-G4013.remedy: AdvanceMonth is monotonic: pass a month equal to or later than the current simulation month. A month regression is rejected, never silently rewound.

MET-G4014.message: checkpoint month {checkpoint} precedes the current month {current}
MET-G4014.remedy: Checkpoint is monotonic: pass a month equal to or later than the current simulation month. A checkpoint before the current month is rejected, never silently rewound.

MET-G4015.message: preview range is inverted: from {fromMonth} to {toMonth}
MET-G4015.remedy: Request a preview whose toMonth is at least fromMonth. An inverted range is rejected, never silently returned empty.

MET-G4016.message: a district cannot be created with an empty name
MET-G4016.remedy: Pass a non-empty district name to CreateDistrict. An empty name is rejected rather than silently stored.

MET-G4017.message: a district must contain at least one cell
MET-G4017.remedy: Pass at least one cell reference to CreateDistrict. A cell set that resolves to nothing would be a resolved-to-empty-set false success (AC-13), so it is rejected.
